content.content:
### Initialization leaves no bad link

(wink + agent, 2026-11-16, from **docs: CONTRIBUTING.md names the project's tasks**) A workspace an
initialization makes should have no bad link, and where one cannot be avoided it says what fixes
it, never leaving the reader a broken link to find. The information a link points at travels with
the agent-files, so the fix is to ship it, not to drop the link.

- **One mechanism** (wink, 2026-11-16). Three set a workspace up today: `vc-x1 init`, `--adopt`
  included, makes the repos and copies no agent-files, `scripts/vc-dr-apply.sh` copies the set,
  the base skeleton, and a language skeleton, and `vc-x1 agent-files copy` copies the set between
  adopters. Two ways to start a workspace is acceptable for now, and not for long: `init` takes
  on what `vc-dr-apply` does and the script retires. Whether `agent-files copy` folds in too is
### init defaults to --local

(wink, 2026-10-30) `vc-x1 init` makes the workspace on the machine and creates and publishes nothing
unless `--push` asks, as `commit` does in **Only push publishes**. Today it creates the remotes and
pushes, public on GitHub unless `--private`, so a bare `init` publishes a repo.

- `--push` is what creates the remotes and publishes, and the approval it needs is the rest of that
  section's. `--private` and `--push-retries` take effect with it.
- Publishing later needs a way: a workspace with no `origin` has nothing for `vc-x1 push` to push to,
  so `push`, or a command of its own, creates the remotes.
- The trailers: `init`'s cross-links then have no URL to stamp, so they take the path form **feat:
  ochid trailers are URLs** defines, `/.agent-session/<chid>`, and they stay valid after a remote
  appears, the URL being checked only on a URL form.
- The name: `--repo local` is already a category, a local directory of bare repos, which is a remote
  of a kind and not this `--local`, so one of the two is renamed or explained. `clone` is to be
  checked for the same default.
  - **feat: close, land, and push compose with testing** makes `init --test-repo <path>/<repo-name>`,
    with local bare remotes, so that name is not taken by `--local`. What a bare `init` does stays here.

### squash-push shows what it takes, and push follows jj

(wink + agent, 2026-10-28) The rules for rewriting what is published, from the opening that became
**feat: undo takes back the last vc-x1 run**. `squash` refuses folding into a commit on the trunk's
remote without `--yes`, a guard on a local act that undo takes back, while `squash-push -s b` folds a
work `@` it expects empty without showing it, and pushes it. The mistake that matters is a command
taking more than was meant and publishing it unseen, not a bookmark moving sideways. After the undo
cycle and before **squash takes --include**, wink's order (2026-10-28).

- Local acts are not refused, since undo takes them back: squash's trunk refusal becomes its
  existing rewrite warning, and its `--yes` retires as `--dev` did, hidden and refused, freeing it
  for **squash takes --include**.
- A command shows what it takes when that is more than the routine: `squash-push -s b` at rest
  expects an empty work `@`, and a non-empty one is listed, each file with `+n -m`, and asked for,
  `squash --include`'s approval. `squash-push.yes` skips the routine case alone, the agent tail or
  an empty work side.
- Pushes are force-with-lease and nothing more: a backward or sideways move goes, undo reversing
  it, and the lease stops a push over a remote someone else moved. No bookmark is special to vc-x1,
  and a shared repo's guard on its trunk is the server's, GitHub's branch protection refusing a
  force push from every client.
- The agent-repo stays clean in one command, `squash-push -s a` folding the tail into its published
  tip, a local rewrite and a leased push.
### Improve init and add rename and delete subcommands

(wink + agent, 2026-10-11) A workspace's name is written into six places, and nothing renames or
removes them together: the work-repo's directory, the agent-repo's directory when it is not
nested, the two repos on the remote, each repo's `origin` URL, the `.vc-config.{toml|md}` of both
sides, and the Claude Code symlink. And `init` makes a workspace it cannot always finish, or that
Claude Code does not find.

- The order is wink's: `init` is fixed first, then `vc-x1 delete`, then `vc-x1 rename`. Each is a
  cycle of its own.
- The `init` work is more than one cycle, wink's order: the path over 200 characters, then the
  name GitHub would change, the order the two parts below are in. The first part, the agent
  template `--use-template` looked for, retired with the flag (2026-11-03).
- Delete is ahead of rename: its "find every part of a workspace from its config" is what rename
### Every repo's .gitignore ignores .claude, and settings stay out of agent-repos

(wink + agent, 2026-10-21) The sandbox Claude Code runs commands in blocks writes to the project's
`.claude/settings.json`, `skills`, `hooks`, and more by mounting `/dev/null` over each, and for a
name that does not exist it first creates an empty read-only file on the host to mount over, seen
from outside as files that come and go during a sandboxed command. jj inside the sandbox skips
them as devices, but a `jj` run outside meanwhile, or after a sandboxed command died, would
snapshot them as new files. vc-x1 shows them since its work repo ignores only
`/.claude/settings.local.json`, narrowed when the agent-repo moved to `.agent-session`, where
`/.claude` had been ignored whole. `.agent-session/.claude` exists too, made by a session run from
inside the agent-repo, with `.cc-writes`.

The rule, wink's calls (2026-10-21):

alone, its trailer naming the agent `@`. `--push` publishes what was committed, as `vc-x1 push`
does, a draft push, and `vc-x1 show -s work -r @-` is the look at it before then. `vc-x1 commit -s
b --title "..." --body "..."` is the same pair for work outside a cycle, where `-r` names a commit
below `@`, described in place with its trailer stamped, and `--bookmark` the bookmark to advance.
Every argument is a flag. What to keep in mind:

- **No checks of the project's own.** vc-x1 runs no build or tests. Validation is the per-rung
  flow's job, run *before* the commit.
- **Rerunning a push is safe.** Push keeps no state and cannot resume: every stage no-ops when its
  work is already done, so a failed run is re-run, not resumed.
- **The trailers are stamped**, never hand-written into `--title` or `--body`.

  positional.
- **Preflight checks the symlink path.** A session started in the directory first makes
  `~/.claude/projects/<mangled-path>` a real directory, holding its transcript and `memory/`, and
  the symlink step refuses a path that "exists and is not a symlink", the last step, after the
  push. Preflight refuses it with nothing made, or init moves the directory's transcripts into the
  new agent-repo and replaces it with the symlink, the session first exited.
- **A directory holding only `.claude/` is adopted without `--adopt`**, since a session started
  there leaves it, or the refusal names `--adopt`.
- **`.claude/` stays out of the initial commit**: the work `.gitignore` ignores only
  `/.claude/settings.local.json`, so an adopted `.claude/.cc-writes/` is committed and pushed. The
  wider rule is **Every repo's .gitignore ignores .claude, and settings stay out of agent-repos**,
  and this needs at least the adopted directory's `.claude/` kept out.
- Related: **init defaults to --local**, a bare `init` publishing a public GitHub repo today, and
  **Initialization leaves no bad link**, init copying no agent-files.
- The acceptance: `vc-x1 init ../hello`, with `--test-repo` and then to GitHub with `--private`,
  in a directory a session was started in, leaves a dual workspace whose symlink holds that
  session's transcript, and nothing of `.claude/` committed.

### feat: squash-push refuses an agent push that names unpublished work

(wink + agent, 2026-11-19) `vc-x1-dev squash-push -s a`, run after a session whose opening pair
was local, pushed the agent `main` with a commit whose `ochid:` named a work commit no pushed ref
reached, a dangling link on the remote, undone by `jj op restore` and a push of `main` back. `-s a`
was At rest's user form before `-s b` replaced it, so the habit is the old rule's.

- `squash-push` and `push`, with `-s a`, refuse an agent push carrying an `ochid:` that names a work
  commit no remote ref reaches, naming each, and say `-s b` pushes the work side first.
- `--yes` pushes anyway, the user's choice, as for a forced push ([Before any
  push](AGENTS.md#before-any-push)).
- The same check is what **feat: a cycle's state is recorded, and every end is durable** calls an
  end not durable, so the two share the test of whether a work commit is reachable from a pushed

I think it should be split. The ladder has grown into three subjects that share little beyond the CLI:

1. **Rungs start and end, stages become subcommands:** `rung start` and `stop`, a commit marking only `(done)`, and the `cycle`/`rung` subcommand migration. The docs half is the per-rung flow's start step, the markers from the set-aside `nruymrqm`, and the renamed invocations.

- **This cycle becomes 1.** Its opening exists only on this machine, so it can be reworked: retitled to, say, **`feat: rung start and end, stages as subcommands`** (47 characters), with the bookmark renamed to match. Its record keeps only 1's problem, solution, acceptance lines, deliberation bullets, and rungs. That's the third rework of the opening, all local, which "may be reworked while local" allows.

Each carries its part of the record as written: the bookmark decisions in one, and the `status`/`list` decisions in the other. Nothing gets re-deliberated, and `cycle open` moves each entry into its record when the time comes.
- **The proposal then follows 1, 2, and 3,** which together supply its rules.

content.text:
Here's how I see cycle 1's design, as the two flows you asked for, with the split mechanics after. Some steps depend on cycle 2, and I've marked them.

**Multi-step cycle**

```
vc-x1 sync -s b
vc-x1 bookmark create -s w                  # (cycle 2) cycle-20261120T150000Z on @, first thing
#   ...look around, deliberate, nothing committed...
vc-x1 cycle open --title "feat: x"          # inherits the bookmark (cycle 2), writes the record,
                                            # zTOC: 0 (current) feat: x opening
#   plan the record, `vc-x1 cycle ladder`, bump to X.Y.Z-0, validate, "please review"
vc-x1 rung commit -s b                      # opening (done), nothing current
vc-x1 rung start                            # zTOC: 1 (current) <first work rung>, uncommitted
#   bump X.Y.Z-1, work, subsection, validate, install dev, "please review"
vc-x1 rung commit -s b --body "..."         # title taken from the current rung, (done), none current
vc-x1 rung start                            # the next rung... repeat start/commit
vc-x1 cycle close -s b --multi-step --trapezoid main
vc-x1 cycle land main -s b                  # local; `--push` with your approval
```

**Single-step cycle**

```
vc-x1 sync -s b
vc-x1 bookmark create -s w                  # (cycle 2) early, before the title is known
vc-x1 cycle open --title "fix: y"           # zTOC: 0 (current) fix: y opening
#   record, the work, bump to the bare X.Y.Z, validate, "please review"
vc-x1 cycle close -s b --single-step --body "..."   # one commit, bare title, zTOC: 0 (done) fix: y
vc-x1 cycle land main -s b
```

There's also the variant where the opening is committed first: `rung commit -s b`, then the work, then `cycle close --single-step`, which squashes the closing into the opening as it does today.

**Until cycle 2 lands:** `cycle open` still makes the bookmark as its first act. That's early, but you can't make the bookmark before you know the title. Today `--bookmark` refuses a name that already exists, so you can't create one by hand and then open on it. Inheriting is cycle 2's job.

**Decisions for cycle 1:**
1. **`rung commit` with no rung current: refuse it**, naming `rung start`. That makes it the strict complement of `start`. Alternatively, `--title` could commit a named rung without starting it, but that brings back the skip you don't want. I lean toward refusing.
2. **`cycle open` starts the opening**, as agreed.
3. **The closing needs no `rung start`.** `cycle close` is its own stage, and it's refused while a work rung is current, so a rung can't be left in flight.
4. **The review word "go":** `rung commit --start` chains the next rung's start. You type it, so `(done)` still doesn't start anything by itself. "commit" means `rung commit` alone.
5. **`rung stop`** clears the marker and leaves the edits alone.

**The split mechanics** (all local):
- Set rung 1's code aside first, as the Unplanned work rule says: a jj commit with a local bookmark.
- `@` is then left holding only `TODO.md` and `zTOC.md`. I rewrite the record as cycle 1's and add the two `## Todo` entries, **feat: the bookmark is made first** and **feat: status and list print @ and @- alike**, ranked first and second ahead of `v0.3.1`, each carrying its deliberation.
- Fold that into the opening with `vc-x1 squash -s b --title "feat: rung start and end, stages as subcommands opening"` and rename the bookmark to match.
- Restore the set-aside code onto it, and continue rung 1.

Do you agree with decisions 1 to 5? If so, should I do the split?

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# cycle-rehearsal.sh - run the cycle flow end to end, by `cycle`'s flags.
#
# Makes a throwaway dual workspace with local bare remotes and no cargo
# project, and runs three cycles through it, open to Land, checking
# what each command left:
#
#   1. a single-step cycle with nothing committed before its closing
#   2. a single-step cycle whose opening is committed first
#   3. a ladder, closed as a trapezoid, with each way back from a fault
#      found after the closing tried: fix inside, fix on top, reopen
#
# Usage: scripts/cycle-rehearsal.sh [DIR]
#   DIR  where the workspace and its remotes go, removed first
#        [default: ~/tmp/cycle-rehearsal]
#   VC   the binary under test [default: vc-x1-dev]
#
# Exits zero when every check passed. The ways back the tool refuses
# are reported, not failed: the rehearsal's job there is to say which.

set -uo pipefail

VC=${VC:-vc-x1-dev}
ROOT=${1:-$HOME/tmp/cycle-rehearsal}
WS=$ROOT/ws
AGENT=$WS/.agent-session
LOG=$ROOT/rehearsal.log
LINK=$HOME/.claude/projects/$(printf '%s' "$WS" | tr '/.' '--')

checks=0
failed=0
refused=()

say() { printf '%s\n' "$*"; }
step() { say; say "== $*"; }

# Run a command that must succeed, its output kept in the log.
run() {
    say "  \$ $*" | tee -a "$LOG"
    if ! "$@" >>"$LOG" 2>&1; then
        say "  FAILED (exit $?): $*, see $LOG"
        failed=$((failed + 1))
        return 1
    fi
}

# Run a command that is expected to be refused, and say which way it went.
tries() {
    local what=$1
    shift
    say "  \$ $*" | tee -a "$LOG"
    if "$@" >>"$LOG" 2>&1; then
        say "  done: $what"
    else
        say "  refused: $what"
        refused+=("$what")
    fi
}

# check <what> <actual> <expected>
check() {
    checks=$((checks + 1))
    if [ "$2" = "$3" ]; then
        say "  ok: $1"
    else
        say "  NOT OK: $1"
        say "    expected: $3"
        say "    actual:   $2"
        failed=$((failed + 1))
    fi
}

# check_has <what> <text> <fragment>
check_has() {
    checks=$((checks + 1))
    case "$2" in
    *"$3"*) say "  ok: $1" ;;
    *)
        say "  NOT OK: $1"
        say "    missing: $3"
        failed=$((failed + 1))
        ;;
    esac
}

jjw() { jj --ignore-working-copy -R "$WS" "$@"; }
jja() { jj --ignore-working-copy -R "$AGENT" "$@"; }
title() { jjw log -r "$1" --no-graph -T 'description.first_line()'; }
cid() { jjw log -r "$1" --no-graph -T 'commit_id'; }
agent_cid() { jja log -r "$1" --no-graph -T 'commit_id'; }
bookmarks() { jjw bookmark list -T 'name ++ "\n"' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' '; }
remote_bookmarks() {
    git -C "$ROOT/remotes/ws.git" for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' refs/heads | tr '\n' ' '
}
above_main() { jjw log -r "$1..$2" --no-graph --reversed -T 'description.first_line() ++ "\n"'; }
nparents() { jjw log -r "$1" --no-graph -T 'parents.len()'; }
ladder() { sed -n '/^## Ladder$/,/^## The TOC$/p' "$WS/zTOC.md" | grep '^- '; }

# What every Land leaves: the destination published in both repos, the
# cycle's bookmark gone from both sides, the record closed, and the
# work repo clean.
check_landed() {
    local name=$1 slug=$2
    check "$name: main is published" "$(cid main)" "$(cid main@origin)"
    check "$name: the agent main is published" "$(agent_cid main)" "$(agent_cid main@origin)"
    check "$name: only main is left locally" "$(bookmarks)" "main "
    check "$name: only main is left on origin" "$(remote_bookmarks)" "main "
    check_has "$name: nothing is in progress" "$(cat "$WS/TODO.md")" \
        "_No cycle currently in progress._"
    check "$name: the work @ is empty" "$(jj -R "$WS" log -r @ --no-graph -T 'empty')" "true"
    check_has "$name: the landed commit names its partner" \
        "$(jjw log -r main --no-graph -T description)" "ochid: "
    : "$slug"
}

step "Workspace: $WS, with $VC"
if [ -L "$LINK" ]; then rm "$LINK"; fi
rm -rf "$ROOT"
mkdir -p "$ROOT"
: >"$LOG"
run "$VC" init --target "$WS" --test-repo "$ROOT/remotes" || exit 1
cd "$WS" || exit 1

cat >TODO.md <<'EOF'
# Todo list

## Continuation notes

_None._

## In Progress

_No cycle currently in progress._

## Todo

### feat: a ladder cycle

The ladder's problem, moved into the record by the open.

## Closed

# References
EOF
cat >zTOC.md <<'EOF'
# TOC

## Ladder

_None._

## The TOC

- [TODO.md](TODO.md): the todo list.
EOF
run "$VC" commit -s b --title "chore: the record's skeleton" --body "The skeleton." \
    --bookmark main --push
check "the skeleton is on main" "$(title main)" "chore: the record's skeleton"

step "Cycle 1: single-step, nothing committed before the closing"
run "$VC" cycle --open --title "feat: one commit"
check "open made the bookmark" "$(bookmarks)" "feat-one-commit main "
check_has "open wrote the scaffold" "$(cat TODO.md)" "### feat: one commit"
check "open wrote the ladder" "$(ladder | head -1)" \
    "- [feat: one commit opening](TODO.md#feat-one-commit-opening)"
echo "one" >work.txt
run "$VC" cycle --close -s b --single-step --body "The problem.

Solution: the one commit." --land main --push
check "one commit above the old main" "$(above_main 'main@origin-' main)" "feat: one commit"
check "the ladder is one unlinked rung" "$(ladder)" "- 0 (done) feat: one commit"
check_has "the record is in Closed" "$(sed -n '/^## Closed$/,$p' TODO.md)" "### feat: one commit"
check_landed "cycle 1" feat-one-commit

step "Cycle 2: single-step, its opening committed first"
base=$(cid main)
run "$VC" cycle --open --title "fix: opened first"
run "$VC" cycle --commit -s b
check "the opening is committed" "$(title @-)" "fix: opened first opening"
check_has "the opening has the default body" "$(jjw log -r @- --no-graph -T description)" \
    'Opens the cycle "fix: opened first".'
opening=$(jjw log -r @- --no-graph -T 'change_id.short(12)')
echo "two" >>work.txt
run "$VC" cycle --close -s b --single-step --default-body
check "the closing is squashed into the opening" "$(above_main "$base" @-)" "fix: opened first"
check "the opening's change is kept" "$(jjw log -r @- --no-graph -T 'change_id.short(12)')" \
    "$opening"
run "$VC" cycle --land main -s b --push
check "the one commit landed" "$(title main)" "fix: opened first"
check_landed "cycle 2" fix-opened-first

step "Cycle 3: a ladder, closed as a trapezoid"
base=$(cid main)
run "$VC" cycle --open --title "feat: a ladder cycle"
check_has "open moved the Todo entry" "$(sed -n '/^## In Progress$/,/^## Todo$/p' TODO.md)" \
    "The ladder's problem, moved into the record by the open."
# Plan two work rungs: a heading each, above the closing's.
sed -i 's/^##### feat: a ladder cycle closing$/##### feat: the first rung\n\nIts intent.\n\n##### feat: the second rung\n\nIts intent.\n\n&/' TODO.md
run "$VC" cycle --ladder
check "the ladder has the rungs planned" "$(ladder | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" "4"
run "$VC" cycle --commit -s b
echo "first" >first.txt
run "$VC" cycle --commit -s b --title "feat: the first rung" --body "Why.

Solution: how."
check "the first rung is done and the second unmarked" "$(ladder | sed -n 2,3p)" \
    "- 1 (done) [feat: the first rung](TODO.md#feat-the-first-rung)
- [feat: the second rung](TODO.md#feat-the-second-rung)"
echo "stray" >stray.txt
tries "a commit whose title is no rung's" \
    "$VC" cycle --commit -s b --title "feat: unplanned" --body "b"
rm stray.txt
echo "second" >second.txt
run "$VC" cycle --commit -s b --title "feat: the second rung" --body "Why.

Solution: how."
check "main has not moved" "$(cid main)" "$base"
run "$VC" push -s b
check "the draft push published the cycle's bookmark" "$(remote_bookmarks)" \
    "feat-a-ladder-cycle main "
run "$VC" cycle --close -s b --multi-step --trapezoid main
check "the closing is titled" "$(title @-)" "feat: a ladder cycle closing"
check "the closing is a merge of two" "$(nparents @-)" "2"
check "every rung is done" "$(ladder | grep -c '(done)')" "4"

step "Cycle 3: the ways back from a fault found after the closing"
say "  fix inside: the fix folded into the closing commit"
echo "inside" >inside.txt
tries "fix inside, by \`squash -s b\`" "$VC" squash -s b
check "the closing holds the fix" "$(jjw file list -r @- 'root:"inside.txt"')" "inside.txt"
check "the closing is still a merge of two" "$(nparents @-)" "2"

say "  fix on top: a rung above the closing"
echo "on top" >ontop.txt
tries "fix on top, by \`cycle --commit\`" \
    "$VC" cycle --commit -s b --title "fix: on top" --body "b"
rm -f ontop.txt

say "  reopen: the closing dropped, a fix rung added, the cycle closed again"
closing=$(cid @-)
tip=$(jjw log -r 'heads(@-- ~ main)' --no-graph -T 'commit_id' 2>/dev/null)
tip=${tip:-$(jjw log -r '@-' --no-graph -T 'parents.map(|p| p.commit_id()).join(" ")' | awk '{print $2}')}
run jj -R "$WS" bookmark set feat-a-ladder-cycle -r "$tip" --allow-backwards
run jj -R "$WS" abandon "$closing"
run jj -R "$WS" new feat-a-ladder-cycle
check_has "the record is in progress again" "$(sed -n '/^## In Progress$/,/^## Todo$/p' TODO.md)" \
    "### feat: a ladder cycle"
sed -i 's/^##### feat: a ladder cycle closing$/##### fix: the fault\n\nIts intent.\n\n&/' TODO.md
echo "fixed" >fix.txt
tries "reopen, a fix rung by \`cycle --commit\`" \
    "$VC" cycle --commit -s b --title "fix: the fault" --body "Why.

Solution: how."
tries "reopen, the closing made again" "$VC" cycle --close -s b --multi-step --trapezoid main
check "the cycle closed again" "$(title @-)" "feat: a ladder cycle closing"
check "the fix is a rung of it" "$(above_main "$base" @- | grep -c '^fix: the fault$')" "1"

step "Cycle 3: the Land"
run "$VC" cycle --land main -s b --push
check "the closing landed" "$(title main)" "feat: a ladder cycle closing"
check "the ladder is under the closing" "$(above_main "$base" main | head -1)" \
    "feat: a ladder cycle opening"
check_landed "cycle 3" feat-a-ladder-cycle

step "Result"
if [ -L "$LINK" ]; then rm "$LINK"; fi
say "  $checks checks, $failed failed, the log in $LOG"
if [ ${#refused[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
    say "  refused by the tool:"
    for r in "${refused[@]}"; do say "    - $r"; done
fi
[ "$failed" -eq 0 ]

19	# are reported, not failed: the rehearsal's job there is to say which.
20	
21	set -uo pipefail
22	
23	VC=${VC:-vc-x1-dev}
24	ROOT=${1:-$HOME/tmp/cycle-rehearsal}
25	WS=$ROOT/ws
26	AGENT=$WS/.agent-session
27	LOG=$ROOT/rehearsal.log
28	LINK=$HOME/.claude/projects/$(printf '%s' "$WS" | tr '/.' '--')
29	
30	checks=0
31	failed=0
32	refused=()
33	
34	say() { printf '%s\n' "$*"; }
35	step() { say; say "== $*"; }
36	
37	# Run a command that must succeed, its output kept in the log.
38	run() {
39	    say "  \$ $*" | tee -a "$LOG"
40	    if ! "$@" >>"$LOG" 2>&1; then
41	        say "  FAILED (exit $?): $*, see $LOG"
42	        failed=$((failed + 1))
43	        return 1
44	    fi
45	}
46	
47	# Run a command that is expected to be refused, and say which way it went.
48	tries() {
49	    local what=$1
50	    shift
51	    say "  \$ $*" | tee -a "$LOG"
52	    if "$@" >>"$LOG" 2>&1; then
53	        say "  done: $what"
54	    else
55	        say "  refused: $what"
56	        refused+=("$what")
57	    fi
58	}
59	
60	# check <what> <actual> <expected>
61	check() {
62	    checks=$((checks + 1))
63	    if [ "$2" = "$3" ]; then
64	        say "  ok: $1"
65	    else
66	        say "  NOT OK: $1"
67	        say "    expected: $3"
68	        say "    actual:   $2"
69	        failed=$((failed + 1))
70	    fi
71	}
72	
73	# check_has <what> <text> <fragment>
74	check_has() {
75	    checks=$((checks + 1))
76	    case "$2" in
77	    *"$3"*) say "  ok: $1" ;;
78	    *)
79	        say "  NOT OK: $1"
80	        say "    missing: $3"
81	        failed=$((failed + 1))
82	        ;;
83	    esac
84	}
85	
86	jjw() { jj --ignore-working-copy -R "$WS" "$@"; }
87	jja() { jj --ignore-working-copy -R "$AGENT" "$@"; }
88	title() { jjw log -r "$1" --no-graph -T 'description.first_line()'; }
89	cid() { jjw log -r "$1" --no-graph -T 'commit_id'; }
90	agent_cid() { jja log -r "$1" --no-graph -T 'commit_id'; }
91	bookmarks() { jjw bookmark list -T 'name ++ "\n"' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' '; }
92	remote_bookmarks() {
93	    git -C "$ROOT/remotes/ws.git" for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' refs/heads | tr '\n' ' '
94	}
95	above_main() { jjw log -r "$1..$2" --no-graph --reversed -T 'description.first_line() ++ "\n"'; }
96	nparents() { jjw log -r "$1" --no-graph -T 'parents.len()'; }
97	ladder() { sed -n '/^## Ladder$/,/^## The TOC$/p' "$WS/zTOC.md" | grep '^- '; }
98	
99	# What every Land leaves: the destination published in both repos, the
100	# cycle's bookmark gone from both sides, the record closed, and the
101	# work repo clean.
102	check_landed() {
103	    local name=$1 slug=$2
104	    check "$name: main is published" "$(cid main)" "$(cid main@origin)"
105	    check "$name: the agent main is published" "$(agent_cid main)" "$(agent_cid main@origin)"
106	    check "$name: only main is left locally" "$(bookmarks)" "main "
107	    check "$name: only main is left on origin" "$(remote_bookmarks)" "main "
108	    check_has "$name: nothing is in progress" "$(cat "$WS/TODO.md")" \
109	        "_No cycle currently in progress._"
110	    check "$name: the work @ is empty" "$(jj -R "$WS" log -r @ --no-graph -T 'empty')" "true"
111	    check_has "$name: the landed commit names its partner" \
112	        "$(jjw log -r main --no-graph -T description)" "ochid: "
113	    : "$slug"
114	}
115	
116	step "Workspace: $WS, with $VC"
117	if [ -L "$LINK" ]; then rm "$LINK"; fi
118	rm -rf "$ROOT"
119	mkdir -p "$ROOT"
120	: >"$LOG"
121	run "$VC" init --target "$WS" --test-repo "$ROOT/remotes" || exit 1
122	cd "$WS" || exit 1
123	
124	cat >TODO.md <<'EOF'
125	# Todo list
126	
127	## Continuation notes
128	
129	_None._
130	
131	## In Progress
132	
133	_No cycle currently in progress._
134	
135	## Todo
136	
137	### feat: a ladder cycle
138	
139	The ladder's problem, moved into the record by the open.
140	
141	## Closed
142	
143	# References
144	EOF
145	cat >zTOC.md <<'EOF'
146	# TOC
147	
148	## Ladder
149	
150	_None._
151	
152	## The TOC
153	
154	- [TODO.md](TODO.md): the todo list.
155	EOF
156	run "$VC" commit -s b --title "chore: the record's skeleton" --body "The skeleton." \
157	    --bookmark main --push
158	check "the skeleton is on main" "$(title main)" "chore: the record's skeleton"
159	
160	step "Cycle 1: single-step, nothing committed before the closing"
161	run "$VC" cycle --open --title "feat: one commit"
162	check "open made the bookmark" "$(bookmarks)" "feat-one-commit main "
163	check_has "open wrote the scaffold" "$(cat TODO.md)" "### feat: one commit"
164	check "open wrote the ladder" "$(ladder | head -1)" \
165	    "- [feat: one commit opening](TODO.md#feat-one-commit-opening)"
166	echo "one" >work.txt
167	run "$VC" cycle --close -s b --single-step --body "The problem.
168	
169	Solution: the one commit." --land main --push
170	check "one commit above the old main" "$(above_main 'main@origin-' main)" "feat: one commit"
171	check "the ladder is one unlinked rung" "$(ladder)" "- 0 (done) feat: one commit"
172	check_has "the record is in Closed" "$(sed -n '/^## Closed$/,$p' TODO.md)" "### feat: one commit"
173	check_landed "cycle 1" feat-one-commit
174	
175	step "Cycle 2: single-step, its opening committed first"
176	base=$(cid main)
177	run "$VC" cycle --open --title "fix: opened first"
178	run "$VC" cycle --commit -s b
179	check "the opening is committed" "$(title @-)" "fix: opened first opening"
180	check_has "the opening has the default body" "$(jjw log -r @- --no-graph -T description)" \
181	    'Opens the cycle "fix: opened first".'
182	opening=$(jjw log -r @- --no-graph -T 'change_id.short(12)')
183	echo "two" >>work.txt
184	run "$VC" cycle --close -s b --single-step --default-body
185	check "the closing is squashed into the opening" "$(above_main "$base" @-)" "fix: opened first"
186	check "the opening's change is kept" "$(jjw log -r @- --no-graph -T 'change_id.short(12)')" \
187	    "$opening"
188	run "$VC" cycle --land main -s b --push
189	check "the one commit landed" "$(title main)" "fix: opened first"
190	check_landed "cycle 2" fix-opened-first
191	
192	step "Cycle 3: a ladder, closed as a trapezoid"
193	base=$(cid main)
194	run "$VC" cycle --open --title "feat: a ladder cycle"
195	check_has "open moved the Todo entry" "$(sed -n '/^## In Progress$/,/^## Todo$/p' TODO.md)" \
196	    "The ladder's problem, moved into the record by the open."
197	# Plan two work rungs: a heading each, above the closing's.
198	sed -i 's/^##### feat: a ladder cycle closing$/##### feat: the first rung\n\nIts intent.\n\n##### feat: the second rung\n\nIts intent.\n\n&/' TODO.md
199	run "$VC" cycle --ladder
200	check "the ladder has the rungs planned" "$(ladder | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" "4"
201	run "$VC" cycle --commit -s b
202	echo "first" >first.txt
203	run "$VC" cycle --commit -s b --title "feat: the first rung" --body "Why.
204	
205	Solution: how."
206	check "the first rung is done and the second unmarked" "$(ladder | sed -n 2,3p)" \
207	    "- 1 (done) [feat: the first rung](TODO.md#feat-the-first-rung)
208	- [feat: the second rung](TODO.md#feat-the-second-rung)"
209	echo "stray" >stray.txt
210	tries "a commit whose title is no rung's" \
211	    "$VC" cycle --commit -s b --title "feat: unplanned" --body "b"
212	rm stray.txt
213	echo "second" >second.txt
214	run "$VC" cycle --commit -s b --title "feat: the second rung" --body "Why.
215	
216	Solution: how."
217	check "main has not moved" "$(cid main)" "$base"
218	run "$VC" push -s b
219	check "the draft push published the cycle's bookmark" "$(remote_bookmarks)" \
220	    "feat-a-ladder-cycle main "
221	run "$VC" cycle --close -s b --multi-step --trapezoid main
222	check "the closing is titled" "$(title @-)" "feat: a ladder cycle closing"
223	check "the closing is a merge of two" "$(nparents @-)" "2"
224	check "every rung is done" "$(ladder | grep -c '(done)')" "4"
225	
226	step "Cycle 3: the ways back from a fault found after the closing"
227	say "  fix inside: the fix folded into the closing commit"
228	echo "inside" >inside.txt
229	tries "fix inside, by \`squash -s b\`" "$VC" squash -s b
230	check "the closing holds the fix" "$(jjw file list -r @- 'root:"inside.txt"')" "inside.txt"
231	check "the closing is still a merge of two" "$(nparents @-)" "2"
232	
233	say "  fix on top: a rung above the closing"
234	echo "on top" >ontop.txt
235	tries "fix on top, by \`cycle --commit\`" \
236	    "$VC" cycle --commit -s b --title "fix: on top" --body "b"
237	rm -f ontop.txt
238	
239	say "  reopen: the closing dropped, a fix rung added, the cycle closed again"
240	closing=$(cid @-)
241	tip=$(jjw log -r 'heads(@-- ~ main)' --no-graph -T 'commit_id' 2>/dev/null)
242	tip=${tip:-$(jjw log -r '@-' --no-graph -T 'parents.map(|p| p.commit_id()).join(" ")' | awk '{print $2}')}
243	run jj -R "$WS" bookmark set feat-a-ladder-cycle -r "$tip" --allow-backwards
244	run jj -R "$WS" abandon "$closing"
245	run jj -R "$WS" new feat-a-ladder-cycle
246	check_has "the record is in progress again" "$(sed -n '/^## In Progress$/,/^## Todo$/p' TODO.md)" \
247	    "### feat: a ladder cycle"
248	sed -i 's/^##### feat: a ladder cycle closing$/##### fix: the fault\n\nIts intent.\n\n&/' TODO.md
249	echo "fixed" >fix.txt
250	tries "reopen, a fix rung by \`cycle --commit\`" \
251	    "$VC" cycle --commit -s b --title "fix: the fault" --body "Why.
252	
253	Solution: how."
254	tries "reopen, the closing made again" "$VC" cycle --close -s b --multi-step --trapezoid main
255	check "the cycle closed again" "$(title @-)" "feat: a ladder cycle closing"
256	check "the fix is a rung of it" "$(above_main "$base" @- | grep -c '^fix: the fault$')" "1"
257	
258	step "Cycle 3: the Land"
259	run "$VC" cycle --land main -s b --push
260	check "the closing landed" "$(title main)" "feat: a ladder cycle closing"
261	check "the ladder is under the closing" "$(above_main "$base" main | head -1)" \
262	    "feat: a ladder cycle opening"
263	check_landed "cycle 3" feat-a-ladder-cycle
264	
265	step "Result"
266	if [ -L "$LINK" ]; then rm "$LINK"; fi
267	say "  $checks checks, $failed failed, the log in $LOG"
268	if [ ${#refused[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
269	    say "  refused by the tool:"
270	    for r in "${refused[@]}"; do say "    - $r"; done
271	fi
272	[ "$failed" -eq 0 ]
273	
</system-reminder>

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, handing the viewer a file to save, or using the viewer's camera, microphone, location, screen or device motion. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus broken CLAUDE.md rules and cleanups where the model's recipe covers them; see /simplify) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option. - Use the max or ultra level only when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask for one, never on your own judgment: they are the costliest reviews and start many reviewer subagents.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. ## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>
