content.text:
Yes, you're right. A squash breaks the agent side unless the tool fixes it up.

**Why it breaks.** Each rung is a pair. Work change `W_i` carries `ochid: A_i`, and agent change `A_i` carries `ochid: W_i`. Squashing `W_1..W_n` into the opening `W_0` keeps `W_0`'s change id, but `W_1..W_n` stop being visible revisions. Every `A_i` with i ≥ 1 then names a change that no longer resolves, so those links dangle.

**Two ways to repair it:**

1. **Squash the agent side too.** Fold `A_1..A_n` into `A_0`, leaving one pair `W_0 ↔ A_0`. It's simple and symmetric, but the agent-repo loses its per-rung session boundaries.
2. **Re-point the agent side.** Re-describe each `A_i` to `ochid: W_0`, and give `W_0` one `ochid:` per agent change, `A_0..A_n`. That's the 1:M shape the agent-files already allow ("several agent commits naming one work commit"). Only the agent descriptions change, not their change ids, so `W_0`'s list stays valid. The agent-repo keeps its per-rung history.

**I recommend 2.** It uses a shape we already sanction and keeps the agent history.

**Under either option:**
- The order matters: rewrite the agent side first, then squash the work side.
- **Refuse the squash when any rung's commit is published.** The work rewrite would be a forced push. Under option 1 the agent side is rewritten too, so a published agent commit also refuses. Under option 2 an agent re-description of a pushed commit forces a push as well, so the agent side gets the same check. `--yes` overrides with your approval. This is the same reachability check as the squash-push Todo, so the two can share it.
- **The tool does this, not a hand `jj describe`.** The "No re-describe without coordinating" rule stays as it is, because these are trailers the tool stamped, on local commits.

**This adds two things to cycle 1:**
- The close-`--squash` rung carries the agent re-point and its tests.
- The docs rung says that a squashed cycle is 1:M on the agent side.

The plain version: squashing the work commits deletes the ids that the agent commits point to. So when `--squash` runs, it also points every agent commit at the one surviving work commit, and refuses if any of the affected commits have already been pushed.

content.content:
The trailers are **stamped by the tool**, `vc-x1 cycle` and `vc-x1 commit`. Never hand-write them
into a commit body or `--title`/`--body`.

## vc-x1 commit and push: what they do and do not do

`vc-x1 cycle --commit -s b --title "..." --body "..."` commits both repos with the title and body,
the pair, stamps their trailers ([above](#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)), rewrites the ladder
into the commit, and stays on this machine. `-s` is required, and `-s w` commits the work repo
alone, its trailer naming the agent `@`. `--push` publishes what was committed, as `vc-x1 push`
does, a draft push, and `vc-x1 show -s work -r @-` is the look at it before then. `vc-x1 commit -s
b --title "..." --body "..."` is the same pair for work outside a cycle, where `-r` names a commit
below `@`, described in place with its trailer stamped, and `--bookmark` the bookmark to advance.
Every argument is a flag. What to keep in mind:

- **No checks of the project's own.** vc-x1 runs no build or tests. Validation is the per-rung
  flow's job, run *before* the commit.
- **Rerunning a push is safe.** Push keeps no state and cannot resume: every stage no-ops when its
  work is already done, so a failed run is re-run, not resumed.
- **The trailers are stamped**, never hand-written into `--title` or `--body`.
- **The agent-repo is a linear journal.** Never create an agent-repo bookmark mirroring a work-repo

content.text:
Yes on the work side, with one catch on the agent side.

**The work-repo:** I agree. A cycle bookmark that has had a draft push is still a draft, which is what "draft" means, so the squash can rewrite it. The next push of that bookmark is then a forced push, and the existing forced-push approval asks about it. The hard line is a rung's commit that has already landed on a target, since that history is permanent. The cycle's own bookmark will usually be the target's line, so the check is "is any of the rungs reachable from a remote target bookmark". The rung commits are local or draft until the Land, so in practice this almost never trips.

**The agent-repo is different.** It has no cycle bookmark: the agent-repo is a linear journal on `main` (`agent-data/jj.md`), and a draft push moves the agent `main` (`src/push.rs:626`). So once a cycle has had a draft push, the agent commits `A_i` are on the published agent `main`. Re-pointing their `ochid:` (or squashing them) rewrites published `main`, which means a forced push of the agent `main`. That hits exactly the case draft pushes are for: a second machine that pulled the cycle would diverge.

**My proposal for `close --squash`:**
- **A work rung landed on a target:** refuse, with no override.
- **A work rung only draft-pushed:** go ahead. The next push of the bookmark is forced, and asks, as today.
- **An agent commit already on `main@origin`:** refuse, naming the forced agent push. `--yes` overrides it, for you to approve.
- **Everything local:** go ahead, with no questions.

The plain version: on the work side, only "already landed" blocks a squash. On the agent side, any commit already pushed to its `main` needs your yes, because the agent-repo has no draft bookmark to hide behind.

Configure the work-repo of a dual repo system. The other repo, we call the agent-repo, is
also a markdown configuration file typically named .vc-config.md.

The code blocks in these config files are in toml format and these blocks are logically
concatenated in the order written here and those become the information used for configuring
the system. The [vc-config.md](vc-config.md) contains the documentation for the
various toml tables used for configuration and it is also used during compilation to define
the valid contents of this file.

The file [vc-config-model.md](vc-config-model.md) is the model: every table and key a workspace
config may carry, each with its default or a typical value. It is generated from the schema, so it
cannot fall behind the keys the binary knows.

- agent [[2]]

[repos]

content.text:
I like it. `rung next` is better than `rung start`: it takes no argument and leaves you no choice of rung, so you can't skip one. Bumping at `next` puts the version where it belongs, at the start of a rung's work, so the dev build under review already carries it. I see three issues.

**1. Who writes the version.** The rule today is "The version is the project's: `vc-x1` never bumps it". `[version]` in `.vc-config.md` only *reads* the line, and `cargo xtask bump` writes it, including `Cargo.lock`. My proposal: add `[version] bump = "cargo xtask bump {ver}"`, and have `rung next --ver X` run it. The project's tool stays the writer and `vc-x1` only invokes it. If the config has no `bump`, `--ver` is refused and you bump by hand as now. The version check at commit stays as it is.

**2. The single-step shortcut puts the bump after the review.** `rung commit --ver 1.2.3` would change `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` after validate and the review. The committed tree would then be one nobody validated, which breaks "validation ran after the last edit". So the bump has to come before the work, which means `rung next` again. I'd make single-step a matter of the final verb instead:

```
cycle plan                       # bookmark first, record and zTOC scaffolded, Cargo.toml untouched
rung next --ver 1.2.3            # the opening current, bumped to the bare version
#   work, validate, "please review"
cycle squash                     # one commit, bare title, record to Closed
```

`cycle squash` then always means "this cycle becomes one commit", whether the branch holds zero rungs or a ladder (with the agent re-point and the refusals we agreed). `cycle close` always means the trapezoid. There's no shape inference and no special meaning for "commit without next".

**3. The closing is a rung too.** It's already in the ladder, so `rung next --ver 1.2.3` reaches it naturally, and `cycle close` (or `squash`) commits it. Every commit is then preceded by a `next` that bumps:

```
cycle plan
rung next --ver 1.2.3-0     # the opening (the plan's review)
rung commit
rung next --ver 1.2.3-1     # repeat next/commit
rung commit
rung next --ver 1.2.3       # the closing
cycle close --trapezoid main   |   cycle squash
```

`rung commit` refuses with no rung current, naming `rung next`, and refuses on the closing rung, naming `close`/`squash`. `rung stop` clears the marker and leaves the edits alone.

The plain version: your shape works with one change. The version must be set before the review, not at the commit, so even a single-step cycle runs `rung next --ver`. It then ends with `cycle squash` instead of a commit, and `vc-x1` bumps by running the project's own bump command.

Shall I write this into cycle 1's record?

content.text:
That works if `rung next` can tell a single-step from an opening, and the version you type can tell it. Under the suffix scheme a bare version (no `-N`) is only ever a cycle's last commit. So:

**Rule:** `rung next --ver 1.2.3` on the opening, with a bare version, makes the opening the whole cycle.

- `rung next` bumps, then rewrites the ladder to a single entry, `0 (current) feat: x`, dropping the " opening" and the closing. You can see the shape in `zTOC.md` before the review.
- `rung commit` then commits it as the single-step: the bare title, `--body` required since it holds the work, the record moved to `## Closed`, and the ladder `0 (done) feat: x`. No `cycle close` is needed.
- **The guard:** if the plan laddered any work rungs, a bare version on the opening is refused. The message names both ways on: remove the rungs, or give `1.2.3-0`.

**The two flows:**

```
# single-step
cycle plan --title "fix: y"
rung next --ver 1.2.3        # bare: the opening is the whole cycle
#   work, validate, "please review"
rung commit --body "..."

# multi-step
cycle plan --title "feat: x"

## In Progress

A cycle's record has one home at a time, and while the cycle runs this is it. The block's shape is
the specimen in [cycle-model.md](agent-data/cycle-model.md), and the rules are in [The In Progress
block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block).

### feat: provisional bookmark, st and list similar

#### Problem

A cycle's bookmark is made by `cycle --open`, which also names it from the title and moves the
title's `## Todo` entry, so a bookmark cannot be made before the title is known, and the habit of a
bookmark first, which keeps a commit or push from reaching a shared line, `main` or a release
branch, has no command of its own. `cycle --status` finds the bookmark by the title's slug alone,
so one named by `--bookmark` is not found. `vc-x1 status` and `vc-x1 list` print the same commit
differently, `status` the change and commit ids and `list` the change id and ochid, at different
lengths, and `list` reads `.` without `-s` where `status` reads the work-repo, so neither confirms
what the other shows. A rung has an end, its commit, and no start: the commit writes the next rung
`(current)` into history before any work on it, a prediction an inserted rung makes false. And the
cycle's stages are flags of one command, where a rung's acts and a cycle's read as two.

#### Solution

`vc-x1 bookmark` with the subcommands `create`, `delete`, `rename`, `move`, and `list`, `create`
with no name making a provisional `cycle-<ts>`, so a bookmark is the first thing made, before any
title. `cycle --open` inherits the bookmark it finds on `@`, refusing one that tracks a remote, and
records its name, which bare `cycle --status` reads. `vc-x1 status` and `vc-x1 list` print each
commit by one formatter, its change id, commit id, and ochid, laid out as `jj st` and `jj log` lay
theirs, both defaulting to the work-repo and a bare `list` showing the `@` and `@-` that `status`
shows. `vc-x1 rung start` starts a rung, marking it `(current)` in the working copy, and `rung
commit` ends it, `(done)`, nothing current until the next start. The stages become subcommands,
`cycle open|close|land|push|status|ladder` and `rung start|stop|commit`, later stages chaining as
flags, the old flags gone. The agent-files say the bookmark is made first, provisional while its
name is unsettled, and why: no shared line is written by accident, and the per-rung flow starts
each rung.

#### Acceptance check

In a fresh `vc-x1 init` workspace, with the cycle's dev build:

- `vc-x1 bookmark create -s w` makes `cycle-<ts>` on `@`, and `cycle --open --title "<title>"`
  inherits it, writing its name into the record, and a bare `cycle --status` names it.
- `vc-x1 bookmark rename -s w cycle-<ts> <name>` moves the bookmark and the record's name, and a
  bare `cycle --status` names `<name>`.
- `cycle --open` refuses on an `@` carrying two local bookmarks, naming both, and on one carrying a
  bookmark that tracks a remote, `main` moved onto it.
- `vc-x1 status -s w` and `jj st` print the same lines for the repo, and `vc-x1 list -s w -r
  <revset>` and `jj log -r <revset>` the same lines, each commit line with its ochid added after
  the commit id.
- From the workspace root and from a subdirectory, a bare `vc-x1 list` shows the work-repo's `@`
  and `@-`, the two commits a bare `vc-x1 status` shows.
- `cycle open` marks the opening `(current)`, `rung commit` marks it `(done)` with no rung current,
  `rung start` marks the next `(current)` in the working copy, and no commit on the cycle's branch
  holds a `(current)` in its `zTOC.md`.
- The rehearsal passes, by the subcommands alone.

#### Deliberation

- **A cycle before `v0.3.1`**: this runs ahead of **agent-files(proposal): v0.3.1**, so the rule
  and the tool arrive together and the proposal carries both.
  - Folded into `v0.3.1` as a rule alone, the rule would describe a habit the tool cannot yet
    support.
  - Its first `--open`, on the bookmark `agent-files-proposal-v031`, was undone for this one, its
    record not yet written.
- **A `bookmark` command, not a provisional `--open`**: making a bookmark is its own command, and
  `--open` inherits it.
  - The state-recording Todo's design, `--open` without `--title`, a `### (untitled)` heading, and a
    later rename, kept the bookmark inside the cycle machinery, so the habit could not run without
    a cycle.
  - It follows jj's `jj bookmark`, so the names are the ones its users know, and it replaces
    `delete-bookmark` and `move-bookmark`.
- **A generated name is renamed by hand alone**: `create` with no name makes `cycle-<ts>`, `<ts>`
  UTC to the second in ISO 8601's basic form, and nothing renames it automatically.
  - The tool never renames a bookmark on its own, so no stage's output depends on whether a name
    was given or generated, and the record needs no `provisional` flag.
  - The cost accepted: a forgotten `cycle-<ts>` keeps its name until someone renames it.
- **`rename` rewrites the record**: renaming the cycle's own bookmark rewrites the name the record
  holds, so a bare `cycle --status` still finds it. `bookmark` knows the record for that one name
  and nothing else.
- **`rename` and `delete` of a pushed bookmark push**: free while local, and with an `origin`
  bookmark each is a push and takes approval.
- **No `set`**: jj's `set` is create or move, which is the move of a shared line the habit guards
  against. `list` is cheap and pairs with the `status` and `list` cleanup.
- **Scope**: `-s w` and `-s p`, `a` and `b` refused, since the agent-repo is a linear journal and
  carries no bookmark.
- **What `--open` inherits**:
  - With `--bookmark <NAME>`, that bookmark when it is on `@`, else it is created.
  - Without it, the one local bookmark on `@`, the slug's created when there is none, and refused
    over two or more, naming each.
  - Never a bookmark that tracks a remote, so a trunk moved onto `@` is refused rather than adopted.
- **The record holds the bookmark**: a `toml` block under the `###` cycle heading, `bookmark =
  "<name>"`, a subset of the state-recording Todo's cycle block, which that cycle extends rather
  than replaces.
- **`status` and `list` agree**: both default `-s` to `work`, and a bare `list` shows `@` and `@-`,
  `-n 2`, the commits `status` shows. Their other options and the other commands' are left for
  later cycles.
- **Both show three ids**: each commit's change id, commit id, and ochid, jj's two and vc-x1's
  pairing, the ochid empty on an uncommitted `@`.
  - jj's two alone would drop the pairing, the one thing vc-x1 adds to a dual repo, and the change
    id and ochid alone would drop the commit id `jj st` shows.
- **No `--retitle` and no `(untitled)`**: with the bookmark made first, `--open` runs once the title
  is known, so neither is needed.
- **A rung is started and ended, the first work rung** (wink, 2026-11-19): the opening's commit
  wrote rung 1 `(current)`, a prediction committed as a fact, which `m-13` accepted to remove and
  the dead-end **fix: a cycle commit marks no rung current** did not land.
  - Inserted as a rung, wink's call, and first, so every later rung is committed by `vc-x1-dev`
    running it, and the opening's own `(current)` dropped by hand in its rework.
  - Removing the marker alone was applied first and is not enough (wink): rung 1 is current while
    its work is in `@`, and only a commit's tree must not say so. A commit ends a rung, and its
    complement starts one, so `(done)` never starts the next.
  - The marker lives in the working copy's `zTOC.md` alone, `rung commit` writing the rung `(done)`
    and none current, and `cycle ladder` keeping a `(current)` it finds and never making one. The
    state-recording cycle moves it into the record's blocks.
  - `cycle open` starts the opening, opening the cycle being starting its first rung.
  - Guessing the rung in flight from a non-empty `@` was weighed and not taken: `@`'s changes need

- **The stages are subcommands** (wink, 2026-11-19): `cycle open|close|land|push|status|ladder` and
  `rung start|stop|commit`, a cycle's acts and a rung's each a command of their own.

    warning, since no other cycle is in flight and none starts before the proposal is done.
  - This record names the stages as they were when each line was written.

## In Progress

A cycle's record has one home at a time, and while the cycle runs this is it. The block's shape is
the specimen in [cycle-model.md](agent-data/cycle-model.md), and the rules are in [The In Progress
block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block).

### feat: one cycle flow, plan, rungs, close

#### Problem

A rung has an end, its commit, and no start: the commit writes the next rung `(current)` into
history before any work on it, a prediction an inserted rung makes false. The version is bumped by
hand at each rung's first step, which the tool checks only at the commit. A cycle's shape is chosen
by two paths through the tool, a single-step's `--close --single-step` and a ladder's `--commit`
rungs and `--close --multi-step`, and a ladder cannot be made one commit afterward, since a squash
discards the change ids the agent commits' `ochid:` trailers name. And the cycle's stages are flags
of one command, where a rung's acts and a cycle's read as two.

#### Solution

One flow for every cycle. `vc-x1 cycle plan` makes the bookmark and scaffolds the record and the
ladder, the version untouched. `vc-x1 rung next --ver <version>` marks the first rung not done
`(current)` in the working copy and bumps the version by the command the config's `[version] bump`
names, and `rung commit` commits it, `(done)` and none current, `rung stop` clearing the marker
instead. A bare version on the opening makes the opening the whole cycle, its ladder one entry and
its `rung commit` the single-step. Otherwise `rung next` reaches the closing like any rung, and
`cycle close` commits it, or `cycle squash` makes the ladder one commit, the agent commits
re-pointed to it. The stages are subcommands, `cycle plan|close|squash|land|push|status|ladder` and
`rung next|stop|commit`, the old flags gone, and the agent-files say so.

#### Acceptance check

In a fresh `vc-x1 init` workspace, with the cycle's dev build:

- `cycle plan --title "<title>"` makes the bookmark, the record, and the ladder, the version line
  unchanged and no rung current.
- `rung next --ver X.Y.Z-0` marks the opening `(current)` and leaves the version line reading

## In Progress

A cycle's record has one home at a time, and while the cycle runs this is it. The block's shape is
the specimen in [cycle-model.md](agent-data/cycle-model.md), and the rules are in [The In Progress
block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block).

### feat: one cycle flow, plan, rungs, close

#### Problem

A rung has an end, its commit, and no start: the commit writes the next rung `(current)` into
history before any work on it, a prediction an inserted rung makes false. The version is bumped by
hand at each rung's first step, which the tool checks only at the commit. A cycle's shape is chosen
by two paths through the tool, a single-step's `--close --single-step` and a ladder's `--commit`
rungs and `--close --multi-step`, and a ladder cannot be made one commit afterward, since a squash
discards the change ids the agent commits' `ochid:` trailers name. And the cycle's stages are flags
of one command, where a rung's acts and a cycle's read as two.

#### Solution

One flow for every cycle. `vc-x1 cycle plan` makes the bookmark and scaffolds the record and the
ladder, the version untouched. `vc-x1 rung next --ver <version>` marks the first rung not done
`(current)` in the working copy and bumps the version by the command the config's `[version] bump`
names, and `rung commit` commits it, `(done)` and none current, `rung stop` clearing the marker
instead. A bare version on the opening makes the opening the whole cycle, its ladder one entry and
its `rung commit` the single-step. Otherwise `rung next` reaches the closing like any rung, and
`cycle close` commits it, or `cycle squash` makes the ladder one commit, the agent commits
re-pointed to it. The stages are subcommands, `cycle plan|close|squash|land|push|status|ladder` and
`rung next|stop|commit`, the old flags gone, and the agent-files say so.

#### Acceptance check

In a fresh `vc-x1 init` workspace, with the cycle's dev build:

- `cycle plan --title "<title>"` makes the bookmark, the record, and the ladder, the version line
  unchanged and no rung current.
- `rung next --ver X.Y.Z-0` marks the opening `(current)` and leaves the version line reading
  `X.Y.Z-0`, and `rung commit` marks it `(done)` with no rung current. No commit on the cycle's
  branch holds a `(current)` in its `zTOC.md`.
- `rung commit` with no rung current is refused, naming `rung next`, and on the closing rung,
  naming `cycle close` and `cycle squash`. `rung next` while a rung is current is refused, and
  `rung stop` clears the marker, the edits left alone.
- A single-step, `cycle plan`, `rung next --ver X.Y.Z`, `rung commit --body`, leaves one commit
  above `main` under the bare title, the record in `## Closed`, and the ladder `0 (done) <title>`.
  A bare version on an opening whose plan has work rungs is refused.
- A ladder closed by `cycle close --trapezoid main` is a merge of two. Closed by `cycle squash`
  instead, it is one commit under the bare title, whose `ochid:` names every agent commit of the
  cycle and each of which names it. `squash` is refused over a rung a target reaches, and without
  `--yes` over an agent commit `main@origin` reaches.
- The rehearsal passes, by the subcommands alone.

  wrote rung 1 `(current)`, a prediction committed as a fact, which `m-13` accepted to remove and
  the dead-end **fix: a cycle commit marks no rung current** did not land.
  - Removing the marker alone was applied first and is not enough (wink): rung 1 is current while
    its work is in `@`, and only a commit's tree must not say so. A commit ends a rung, and its
    complement starts one, so `(done)` never starts the next.

    and none current, and `cycle ladder` keeping a `(current)` it finds and never making one. The
    state-recording cycle moves it into the record's blocks.

    not be the next rung's.
- **`rung next`, not `rung start`** (wink, 2026-11-20): it takes no rung, marking the first not

### feat: the bookmark is made first

(wink + agent, 2026-11-19, split from **feat: one cycle flow, plan, rungs, close** 2026-11-20) A
cycle's bookmark is made by `cycle --open`, which also names it from the title and moves the
title's `## Todo` entry, so a bookmark cannot be made before the title is known, and the habit of a
bookmark first, which keeps a commit or push from reaching a shared line, `main` or a release
branch, has no command of its own. `cycle --status` finds the bookmark by the title's slug alone,
so one named by `--bookmark` is not found. The stage names below are the ones **feat: one cycle
flow, plan, rungs, close** lands, `--open` becoming `cycle plan`.

- **Solution**: `vc-x1 bookmark` with the subcommands `create`, `delete`, `rename`, `move`, and
  `list`, `create` with no name making a provisional `cycle-<ts>`, so a bookmark is the first thing
  made, before any title. `cycle plan` inherits the bookmark it finds on `@`, refusing one that
  tracks a remote, and records its name, which a bare `cycle status` reads. The agent-files say the
  bookmark is made first, provisional while its name is unsettled, and why: no shared line is
  written by accident.
- **Acceptance check**, in a fresh `vc-x1 init` workspace with the cycle's dev build:
  - `vc-x1 bookmark create -s w` makes `cycle-<ts>` on `@`, and `cycle plan --title "<title>"`
    inherits it, writing its name into the record, and a bare `cycle status` names it.
  - `vc-x1 bookmark rename -s w cycle-<ts> <name>` moves the bookmark and the record's name, and a
    bare `cycle status` names `<name>`.
  - `cycle plan` refuses on an `@` carrying two local bookmarks, naming both, and on one carrying a
    bookmark that tracks a remote, `main` moved onto it.
- **Rungs, provisional**: **feat: vc-x1 bookmark and its subcommands**, `delete-bookmark` and
  `move-bookmark` replaced; **feat: cycle plan inherits the bookmark on @**, the record's name read
  by every stage, and the scaffold no longer claiming a `## Todo` entry when there was none;
  **docs: the bookmark is made first**, Opening, Cycles run on a bookmark and its why, jj.md's
  Create, and `cycle-model.md`'s Who writes what.
- **A `bookmark` command, not a provisional `--open`**: making a bookmark is its own command, and
  `cycle plan` inherits it.
  - The state-recording Todo's design, `--open` without `--title`, a `### (untitled)` heading, and a
    later rename, kept the bookmark inside the cycle machinery, so the habit could not run without
    a cycle.
  - It follows jj's `jj bookmark`, so the names are the ones its users know, and it replaces
    `delete-bookmark` and `move-bookmark`.
- **A generated name is renamed by hand alone**: `create` with no name makes `cycle-<ts>`, `<ts>`
  UTC to the second in ISO 8601's basic form, and nothing renames it automatically.
  - The tool never renames a bookmark on its own, so no stage's output depends on whether a name
    was given or generated, and the record needs no `provisional` flag.
  - The cost accepted: a forgotten `cycle-<ts>` keeps its name until someone renames it.
  - `cycle plan` without an inherited bookmark or `--bookmark` makes `cycle-<ts>` too, or the
    title's slug as today, to be decided (wink suggested `cycle-<ts>`, 2026-11-20).
- **`rename` rewrites the record**: renaming the cycle's own bookmark rewrites the name the record
  holds, so a bare `cycle status` still finds it. `bookmark` knows the record for that one name
  and nothing else.
- **`rename` and `delete` of a pushed bookmark push**: free while local, and with an `origin`
  bookmark each is a push and takes approval.
- **No `set`**: jj's `set` is create or move, which is the move of a shared line the habit guards
  against. `list` is cheap and pairs with the `status` and `list` cleanup.
- **Scope**: `-s w` and `-s p`, `a` and `b` refused, since the agent-repo is a linear journal and
  carries no bookmark.
- **What `cycle plan` inherits**:
  - With `--bookmark <NAME>`, that bookmark when it is on `@`, else it is created.
  - Without it, the one local bookmark on `@`, a new one made when there is none, and refused
    over two or more, naming each.
  - Never a bookmark that tracks a remote, so a trunk moved onto `@` is refused rather than adopted.
- **The record holds the bookmark**: a `toml` block under the `###` cycle heading, `bookmark =
  "<name>"`, a subset of the state-recording Todo's cycle block, which that cycle extends rather
  than replaces.
- **No `--retitle` and no `(untitled)`**: with the bookmark made first, `cycle plan` runs once the
  title is known, so neither is needed.

### feat: status and list print @ and @- alike

(wink + agent, 2026-11-19, split from **feat: one cycle flow, plan, rungs, close** 2026-11-20)
`vc-x1 status` and `vc-x1 list` print the same commit differently, `status` the change and commit
ids and `list` the change id and ochid, at different lengths, and `list` reads `.` without `-s`
where `status` reads the work-repo, so neither confirms what the other shows. Likely a single-step
cycle.

- **Solution**: one commit line, the change id, commit id, ochid, bookmarks, and description, made
  by one formatter both commands call. `vc-x1 status` prints each repo's lines as `jj st` does, its

I renamed the rung **"feat: a bare version, however set, makes a single-step"**. That's your idea with "ss" spelled out, since the record avoids abbreviations. Say if you'd rather have your wording verbatim.

The design changes with it:
- **`rung commit` decides the shape.** It reads the version line that `[version]` points to, so a version you bump by hand counts the same as one set by `rung next --ver X.Y.Z`.
- **`rung next --ver` with a bare version** also rewrites the ladder to one entry straight away, so the shape shows before the review.
- **A workspace without `[version]`** has no version to read, so its single-step goes through `cycle squash` instead.
- **The acceptance check** gains the by-hand case: bump to the bare version yourself, run a plain `rung next`, then `rung commit --body`.

I updated the solution, the deliberation, the acceptance check and the rung's subsection to match, and regenerated the ladder. These edits sit in the working copy with rung 1's code, so rung 1's commit will carry them. The committed opening still has the old rung title, which is how later rungs are meant to revise the record.

## version.file

The file that holds the project's version, relative to the config file's directory, for the check
`vc-x1 commit` and `vc-x1 cycle` make of a work commit: one that changes no line of this file
starting with `version.pattern` is refused, and `--same-version` commits it as it is. The tool
reads the line and never writes it, the version and its bump being the project's. Both keys or
neither: without them nothing is checked. Owned by the work side because the version is the
artifact's.

```toml
[version.file]
homes = ["workspace-code"]
kind = "str"
doc = "The file holding the version, whose change a work commit is checked for"
used-by = "vc-x1 commit, vc-x1 cycle --commit and --close"
example = "Cargo.toml"
```

## version.pattern

What the version's line in `version.file` starts with, at its left margin, so a line that only
holds the text, a dependency's own `version = ` inside a table, is not taken for it.

```toml
[version.pattern]
homes = ["workspace-code"]
kind = "str"
doc = "What the version's line starts with, in `version.file`"
used-by = "vc-x1 commit, vc-x1 cycle --commit and --close"
example = "version = "
```

The body `vc-x1 cycle --commit` writes on a cycle's opening commit, its first, when `--body` is
        chain in their order, `cycle --close --multi-step --land <BOOKMARK> -s b\n\
        --push`, the\n\
        Land's checks made before the closing is. --push with --land\n\
        publishes the destination and deletes the cycle's bookmark on\n\
        origin, and without --land it is the draft push.\n\n\
        --push alone is a stage: it publishes what the cycle's state calls\n\
        for. A cycle in progress, or closed and not landed, is a draft, and\n\
        its bookmark is pushed. A cycle landed here publishes the target its\n\
        landmark is on and deletes the cycle's bookmark on origin, and with\n\
        nothing to publish it says so. -s is required, `b` or `p`.\n\n\
        --status says where the cycle stands and changes nothing: the\n\
        title, the bookmark and whether it is on the work @, the commits on\n\
        the branch and how many are not pushed, the ladder as the rungs and\n\
        the commits make it, a note when zTOC.md's differs, and the stage\n\
        that comes next. What another stage would refuse, it says.\n\n\
        The version is the project's, and no stage writes it. With `[version]\n\
        file` and `pattern` in the config, --commit and --close refuse a\n\
        commit that changes no line of the file starting with the pattern,\n\

Set the package version in Cargo.toml, its comments and layout kept,
and refresh Cargo.lock in the same step, the build being --locked.

`next` adds one to the suffix's last number, 0.85.22-8 to 0.85.22-9,
and gives a bare version its first, -0. `bare` drops the suffix, a
close-out's version. Anything else is the version as written, X.Y.Z
or X.Y.Z-<suffix>, with one `-` at most and no `+`.

Usage: cargo xtask bump <next|bare|VERSION>

Arguments:
  <next|bare|VERSION>
          `next`, `bare`, or the version as written

Options:

# Process-spawn ban, since 0.79.0. The mechanism, the ban as config,
# the grant as an attribute, this comment as the register, is
# explained in README.md under "No process spawns". A new
# `Command::new` site needs an entry below and a visible
# `#[allow(clippy::disallowed_methods)]` naming it.
#
# The register, closed (wink, 2026-08-19), reopened for entries 5,
# 6, and 7:
#
# 1. Version gate: the `jj -V` probe (src/version.rs). The gate
#    exists to compare the user's jj CLI against our jj-lib, so the
#    CLI spawn is its subject matter.
# 2. Closed 2026-10-20 by the "feat: vc-x1 commit, install, and
#    run-dev" cycle: push's `$EDITOR` launch (src/push.rs) went with
#    push's message stage, since `commit` carries the description
#    and push publishes what was reviewed. The number stays so the
#    later entries keep theirs.
# 3. Init's gh provisioning (src/init.rs): `gh auth status`,
#    `gh repo view`, `gh repo create`. Creating a repo on GitHub is
#    the forge's REST API, not a version-control operation, and no jj or
#    git library can do it, and gh is GitHub's authenticated client.
# 4. Test helpers (src/test_helpers.rs and tests/common/mod.rs):
#    real-jj/git fixture setup and interop verification, kept
#    deliberately independent of the facade under test, and never a
#    substitute for asserting our jj-lib paths directly. The CLI
#    tests' launcher spawning the built vc-x1 binary is this entry
#    too: spawning the binary is what a CLI test is. So is
#    tests/cli_fixture_builder.rs running the dr-1 fixture builder
#    with that binary, which keeps the builder in step with it. So
#    is tests/common/mod.rs's `cargo()`, building the scratch
#    workspaces tests/cli_xtask.rs copies xtask/ into.
# 5. A configured command list (src/command_list.rs): runs the
#    workspace's `[validate]` commands for validate, its `[build]`
#    commands for build, `--dev` or not, and its optional `[install]`
#    lists for install, `--dev` or not, which is each list's whole
#    job. Opened 2026-08-21 by the "empty custom-family into the
#    pinned set and config" cycle, whose plan put the checklist
#    commands in config for one subcommand to run, and widened to the
#    build and install lists by "feat: vc-x1 install stages, deploys,
#    and runs builds", the one site moved out of src/validate.rs so
#    they all share it.
# 6. Sync's remote look (src/jj/session.rs, `git_command`): two
#    git commands that ask a remote and move no ref. `git ls-remote
#    --heads <remote>` gives the commit each of the remote's
#    bookmarks is on, and `git fetch --refmap= --no-tags
#    --no-write-fetch-head` downloads the commits of the ones that
#    moved, so a fast-forward can be told from a rewrite before
#    anything is fetched. Sync has to know what a fetch would do
#    before it makes one, and a fetch changes the repo. jj-lib has no
#    such query: it spawns git itself for its network legs and keeps
#    that layer private, and it builds gix with no network client,
#    as of 0.45.1 and 0.46.0. Opened 2026-10-09 (wink) by the
#    "feat: sync is safe by default" cycle, and temporary: the entry
#    closes when jj-lib offers the query (TODO.md > ## Waiting).
# 7. The workspace's builds (src/install_cmd.rs, src/run_cmd.rs):
#    install, `--dev` or not, runs the binary it is about to copy,
#    `-V` alone, to report the version and commit it shows beside the
#    manifest, run, `--dev` or not, runs the build with the arguments,
#    which is each command's whole job, and the completion forward
#    asks the build, in clap's completion mode, for its own words.
#    Opened 2026-10-21 by "feat: vc-x1 install stages, deploys, and
#    runs builds", and widened to run, run-dev, and the forward by its
#    run rung.
#
# jj-lib's own git children (fetch/push/clone network legs, the
# default-branch query) are jj-lib's implementation detail, not
# vc-x1 spawn sites, and no lint here sees them.
#
# Environment-write ban, since 0.84.35 (bug 21 in notes/bugs.md).
# Tests run as threads of one process, so a write to its environment
# is seen by every test running beside it: `HOME` set to `/h` by one
# test had git look for the signing key under `/h` in another, and
# the jj children the sync tests spawn find no config. A new
# `set_var` / `remove_var` site needs an entry below and a visible
# `#[allow(clippy::disallowed_methods)]` naming it.
#
# The register:
#
# 1. `init::tests::expand_vars_envvar` (src/init/tests.rs): sets
#    and removes `VC_X1_TEST_EXPAND_VAR`, which no other test reads.
# 2. `keep_env_preserves_fixture_across_drop` (tests/cli_keep.rs):
#    sets and removes `VC_X1_TEST_KEEP`, the only test in its own
#    test binary, so no other test shares its process.
    root: &Path,
    command: &str,
    env: &[(&str, &str)],
    vars: &[(&str, &str)],
    lists: &[(&str, &[String])],
    label: &str,
) -> Result<std::process::ExitStatus, String> {
    let words = expand(command, vars, lists).map_err(|e| format!("{label}: `{command}`: {e}"))?;
    let Some((program, args)) = words.split_first() else {
        return Err(format!("{label}: an empty command element"));
    };
    // Register entry 5 (clippy.toml): a configured command list,
    // `[validate]`'s, `[build]`'s, or `[install]`'s, is run as the
    // user would type it, which is the whole job of the commands that
    // run one.
    #[allow(clippy::disallowed_methods)]
    let mut cmd = std::process::Command::new(program);
    cmd.args(args).current_dir(root).envs(env.iter().copied());
    cmd.status().map_err(|e| {
        format!(
            "{label}: cannot run `{command}` from '{}': {e}",
            root.display()
        )
    })
}

/// Render an exit status for the failure message: the code when
/// there is one, else the raw status (a signal on Unix).
fn describe_status(status: std::process::ExitStatus) -> String {
    match status.code() {
        Some(code) => format!("exit {code}"),
        None => format!("{status}"),
    }
}

# vc-config: settable configuration keys

This file is two things at once, and that is the point: the **schema prototype** vc-x1 is built
from, and the **long-form documentation** every generated `reference:` url lands on. One `##`
section per settable key holds that key's prose and, in a `toml` fence, that key's metadata, so
the documentation and the schema cannot describe different keys.

It is not a config file. Your workspace's config is `.vc-config.md` (note the leading dot).
Editing this file changes what the binary knows, takes effect on the next build, and is reviewed
like any source change.

## How this file is read

The format is the config markdown carrier's own: the `toml` fences, concatenated in document
order, form the TOML that gets parsed. build.rs shares the filter (`src/md_fence.rs`) with the
instance-config loader, so the prototype and a `.vc-config.md` are read by one rule, and prose
outside the fences never reaches a parser.

The tag must be exactly `toml`. A fence tagged anything else, or tagged not at all, is prose like
the text around it and never reaches the parser, which is what lets one of these files show a
specimen config in a `text` fence without the specimen becoming configuration.

Shape: one TOML table per settable key, named by the key's path, dynamic segments quoted
(`[repo.category."<cat>"]`). Key order here is rendering order everywhere downstream. The
entries a key's table may carry:

- `homes`: which config file(s) may contain the key. vc-x1 writes it only into those files, and
  `vc-x1 config --validate` reports it as unknown anywhere else. The values:
  - `"user"`: the user-wide config, `~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml` (or
    `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/vc-x1/config.toml`). One per user, still TOML rather than markdown
  - `"workspace-code"`, `"workspace-agent"`: the work side's and the agent side's instance config
- `kind`: value shape, one of `"str"`, `"usize"`, `"bool"`, `"item-list"` (a comma-separated
  list in one string), `"str-list"` (a TOML array of strings, one element per item)
- `doc`: one-line description (rendered into generated configs, so keep it tight)
- `used-by`: what reads the value once it is set, which is a different question from `homes`:
  the command or flag it feeds, or the structural role it plays
- `default`: the built-in value, omitted when there is none
- `example`: representative value for keys with no default
- `required`: active (not commented) in generated configs. The value is role-specific, filled by
  `init`

`--open` opens a cycle. It makes the bookmark on the work `@` first, so every edit of the cycle
is on its branch, and then writes the cycle's record into the working copy. The bookmark is the
slug of `--title`, the anchor a heading of the title gets: lowercase, `-` and `_` kept, each space
a `-`, everything else dropped, so `feat: no trunk, every target is named` names
`feat-no-trunk-every-target-is-named`. `--bookmark` names it instead. A name in use, locally or on
`origin`, is refused, since a new one would move or shadow it. `@` may hold edits, which become
the opening's, a `main` not where its `origin` was last fetched is a warning, the agent repo gets
no bookmark, being on `main` alone, and nothing is pushed. The record:

- In `TODO.md`, what `## Closed` holds is deleted, its intro kept, and the `## Todo` entry titled
  as `--title` is moved into an `## In Progress` scaffold: the title, the item headings, the
  entry's text under Problem, and the opening and closing rung subsections. No entry of that title
  is an empty scaffold, and says so.
- In `zTOC.md`, the ladder is replaced with the opening, current, and the closing.

Everything is planned before anything is made, so a cycle in progress, a workspace with no
`TODO.md` or `zTOC.md`, a `TODO.md` with no `## In Progress`, and a name in use are each refused
with the workspace as it was, the first naming the two files a cycle needs. `--no-record` and
`--bookmark` without `--title` get the bookmark alone, a branch that `--commit` and `--close`
will not take, since they read the cycle from its record. Nothing
is committed or pushed, and the version is the project's to bump: the tool never writes it. A
reference definition only `## Closed` cited is left, for `check anchors` to name. `-R` is
optional and says where, a workspace or a plain repo.

`--ladder` makes the ladder in `zTOC.md` from the rung headings of the cycle in progress, the
`##### ` headings under `#### Rungs` in `TODO.md`, in their order. A rung is written once, as its
heading, and its line and its marker are made:

```
- 0 (done) [feat: a cycle opening](TODO.md#feat-a-cycle-opening)
- [feat: one rung](TODO.md#feat-one-rung)
- [feat: a cycle closing](TODO.md#feat-a-cycle-closing)
```

A rung is `(done)`, numbered by its position, when a commit of its title is on the cycle's branch,
and every other rung is its link alone, so the first unmarked rung is the next and no line claims
work not yet begun. A `(current)` marker, which a `vc-x1` before 0.85.26 wrote on the next rung,
is read as a rung and rewritten without it. A single-step cycle, its one commit under the bare
cycle title, is one unlinked rung. The branch is the commits the cycle's bookmark reaches, and those above it up to the work `@-`, that no other
local bookmark reaches, so no destination is named. The bookmark is the slug of the title in `##
In Progress`, or `--bookmark`'s.

The grammar is strict, and each of these is refused with nothing edited: a commit on the branch
whose title is no rung's, so an unplanned rung gets its heading before its commit, a rung written
twice, a ladder whose first rung is not the cycle title plus " opening" or whose last is not it
plus " closing", and a line of the ladder already there that is not a rung, a left-margin `- `
with a number and marker or neither and a link whose slug is its title's. A done rung below one
not done is a warning. `--dry-run` prints the ladder and writes none.

`--commit` commits the working copies as a rung of the cycle in progress, by the code
[`commit`](#commit) runs, so a dual workspace gets the pair, each half stamped with the other's
change id, and a plain repo one commit with no trailer.

- A cycle's first commit is its opening, which the tool sees and no flag says. Its title is the
  cycle title plus " opening" and its body `[opening] body` from the config, `{title}` the cycle
  title, or a body naming the cycle and its record when the key is absent. A `--body` given takes
  its place.
- Any other commit is a work rung, which gives `--title`, a rung heading under `#### Rungs` not yet
  committed, and `--body`, the text or `@PATH`.
- The ladder is rewritten first, the rung done and the next current, so `zTOC.md` at the commit
  shows the cycle as of it, and it is put back when the commit is not made.
- The cycle's bookmark is the one advanced, the slug of the title in `## In Progress` or
  `--bookmark`'s, so no other bookmark on the line moves.

`-s` is required: `b` makes the pair, `w` the work half with the agent half left to `push`, and
`p` a plain repo's commit. A scope the workspace does not fit, `p` in a dual workspace or `b` in a
plain repo, is refused. `--push` publishes the rung on the cycle's bookmark, a draft
push. Refused before the ladder is written: a title that is no rung's, a rung committed already,
which [`squash`](#squash) continues, the closing's title, an empty work `@`, and a work rung with
no title or body. `--dry-run` prints the descriptions and commits nothing.

`--close [REV,...]` closes the cycle in progress from the work `@`, which is on the cycle's tip,
the bookmark on `@` or `@-`. The acceptance check is run first, by hand, and again after. The
cycle's shape is named, `--single-step` or `--multi-step`, one of them required, and the
branch's commit count checks it:

content.content:
tmp/candidate/vc-x1 cycle --land main -s b --dry-run   # the steps it would take
tmp/candidate/vc-x1 cycle --land main -s b --push      # the tree tested, landed and published
cargo xtask install --release              # now on main, the same build under the plain name
cmp tmp/candidate/vc-x1 ~/.cargo/bin/vc-x1  # the binary tested is the one installed
```

The plain `vc-x1` on the PATH is left to what is on `main` until the Land, so whatever relies on it
never runs a candidate, and the candidate makes its own Land. A binary embeds its commit and
whether the tree was clean, no time, so the build after the fast-forward is the build tested.

`--status` says where the cycle stands, and changes nothing:

```
cycle: feat: a cycle
bookmark: feat-a-cycle, on the work @-
commits: 2 on the branch, 1 not pushed
work @: holds changes
ladder:
  - 0 (done) feat: a cycle opening
  - 1 (done) feat: one rung
  - feat: a cycle closing
next: `cycle --close -s <SCOPE> --multi-step` makes the closing, `--trapezoid <BOOKMARK>` a merge
```

The ladder is the one the rung headings and the commits make, with a note when `zTOC.md`'s
differs, and `next` is the stage the cycle is at: the opening, the next rung by its title, the
closing, or the Land of a cycle closed and not yet landed. What another stage would refuse, a
commit that is no rung's among them, is said and refuses nothing here.

The version is the project's, and no stage writes it. A project that wants a rung's bump checked
names the file that holds its version and what the version's line starts with:

```toml
[version]
file = "Cargo.toml"
pattern = 'version = '
```

`--commit` and `--close`, and [`commit`](#commit) for a work commit, then refuse a commit that
changes no line of the file starting with the pattern, before anything is written, and
`--same-version` commits it as it is. The line is matched at its left margin, so a dependency's
`version = ` inside a table is not the version's. Without the keys nothing is checked, and a
project with no manifest names a file of its own.

This project's own bump is an xtask, outside `vc-x1`: `cargo xtask bump next` adds one to the
version's suffix in `Cargo.toml`, `cargo xtask bump bare` drops the suffix for a close-out, and
`cargo xtask bump <VERSION>` sets it as written, each keeping the manifest's comments and layout
and refreshing `Cargo.lock`, the build being `--locked`. `cargo xtask version` prints it, and
`cargo xtask -h` lists the tasks.

The xtask completes its own tasks. `cargo xtask completions [NAME...]` prints a bash function
that holds no task names: on each tab it asks the xtask of the repo the shell is in, so one copy
serves every repo whose xtask answers clap's completion requests, and a repo with none completes
nothing.

```bash
cargo xtask completions cx > ~/.config/cargo-xtask-completion.bash  # once, cx a shell alias
source ~/.config/cargo-xtask-completion.bash                        # in the shell's startup file
cargo xtask b<TAB>      # bump
cx bump <TAB>           # next bare
```

`cargo xtask <TAB>` reaches the function through cargo's own bash completion, which hands a
subcommand it does not know to the completion registered for `cargo-<name>`, so it needs cargo's
script completing `cargo`, not another completer's, and bash-completion 2.12 or later. A `NAME`,
an alias for `cargo xtask`, is completed directly and needs neither. A request takes about 50
ms once the xtask is built, and the first after its source changes waits for the build.

`scripts/cycle-rehearsal.sh` runs the flow end to end: it makes a throwaway dual workspace with
local remotes and no cargo project under `~/tmp/cycle-rehearsal`, runs two single-step cycles and
a ladder through these flags, open to Land, checks what each command left, and tries each way
back from a fault found after a closing, naming the ones the tool refuses. `VC` names the binary,
`vc-x1-dev` by default.

### trailers

Rewrite a range of work commits' trailers to what is stamped today ([Cross-repo
Linking](#cross-repo-linking-with-git-trailers)), only their descriptions changing, each tree checked
unchanged. It is how a cycle or a test repo moves to a new protocol, and a Land runs the same pass.

```bash
vc-x1 trailers --update --range main..@- --dry-run   # print each description, a cycle's
vc-x1 trailers --update --range main..@-             # rewrite them
vc-x1 trailers --update --range ..@- --ignore-immutable  # a whole history, main@origin's included
```

Each `ochid:` becomes the 12-character change id, an older 8 or 32-character id or a SHA naming one
agent commit being expanded, with `orepo:` stamped above it and any `ocid:` and `pcid:` removed. No

Rung 1, **feat: vc-x1 rung next, stop and commit**, is ready for your review. Full validation, the cycle tests and the rehearsal (48 of 48 checks) all pass. The dev build is installed, and I've used it on this cycle: rung 1 is marked `(current)` in `zTOC.md`.

**The commands:**
- **`vc-x1 rung next [--ver V]`** marks the first rung not done `(current)` in the working copy's `zTOC.md`, and is refused while a rung is current. With `--ver`, it first runs the config's new `[version] bump` command (`cargo xtask bump {ver}` here). If the bump fails, no rung is marked.
- **`vc-x1 rung stop`** clears the marker and leaves your edits alone.
- **`vc-x1 rung commit -s b [--body]`** commits the current rung under its own title, using the same code as `cycle --commit`. The committed ladder marks it `(done)` with nothing current.
  - It's refused when no rung is current (naming `rung next`) and on the closing (naming `cycle --close`).

**Changes to the existing stages:**
- `cycle --ladder` keeps a `(current)` it finds and never makes one.
- Every commit writes no `(current)`: `cycle --commit`, `cycle --close` and `rung commit`.
- `cycle --status` shows the rung in progress and how to commit it, or names `rung next`.
- `cycle --close` is refused while any rung other than the closing is current.
- `cycle --open`'s closing message now points to `rung next --ver`.

**Decision for you:** running the bump command means `vc-x1` now launches an outside program, which the process-spawn register in `clippy.toml` must list. I added it as entry 8, reopening the register you closed. The command is split at whitespace and run without a shell, from the workspace root. Say if you'd rather handle it differently.

**Also changed:**
- The `version.bump` key is in the schema (`vc-config.md`), the regenerated `vc-config-model.md`, and this workspace's `.vc-config.md`.
- README: the ladder now shows the marker, and there's a new `### rung` section.
- Tests: two new ones (the full next/stop/commit/close flow, and `--ver` refused without a `bump` command), plus updated marker tests in `record.rs`.
- The record: rung 1's subsection and the continuation notes.

The new code is mainly `src/cycle/rung.rs`, plus `src/cycle/record.rs` and `src/cycle.rs`.

content.text:
Yes. `vc-x1 cycle --ladder` builds `zTOC.md`'s ladder from `TODO.md`'s `##### ` headings under `#### Rungs`. On your workspace it refuses before it gets that far:

```
error: cycle --ladder: the cycle's bookmark 'feat-one-cycle-flow-plan-rungs-close' is not in ~/tmp/tv0-85-26-1-c031
```

**Why it refuses:**
1. **No cycle bookmark.** `--ladder` marks a rung `(done)` by matching commit titles on the cycle's branch, so it looks for the bookmark named by the title's slug. `cycle --open` makes that bookmark, but this record was written by hand, so there isn't one. `rung next` needs the bookmark for the same reason.
2. **The rungs would then be refused**, from reading the code:
   - The first heading must be the cycle title plus " opening", and the last the title plus " closing". Here that's `feat: one cycle flow, plan, rungs, close opening` and `... closing`.
   - `Mult-step test` is written twice, which is refused on its own.

**The simplest test is to let the tool write the scaffold:**
1. In `TODO.md`, set `## In Progress` back to `_No cycle currently in progress._`.
2. Put the test in `## Todo` as `### feat: multi-step test`. A Conventional Commit title avoids a warning.
3. Run `vc-x1-dev cycle --open --title "feat: multi-step test" -R ~/tmp/tv0-85-26-1-c031`. That makes the bookmark, moves the Todo entry into the record, and writes the opening and closing headings and the ladder.
4. Add `##### feat: create abc.txt` and `##### feat: create def.txt` between the opening and closing headings.
5. Run `vc-x1-dev cycle --ladder`, then `rung next --ver 0.0.1-0`. That needs a `[version]` table in this workspace's `.vc-config.md`; without one, use a bare `rung next`.

**A finding from this:** if `TODO.md` is the gospel, `--ladder` could work without the bookmark when nothing is committed yet, since no rung can be done then. Today it refuses. I can add that to rung 1, or file it as a finding; your call.

I ran `vc-x1-dev cycle --ladder` in your test workspace. Your ladder already matched the four rungs, so it reported nothing to change. I didn't run `rung next`.

**How `rung next` updates the version:** it doesn't, unless the config tells it how. `vc-x1` never guesses how a project versions itself, and it doesn't read `CONTRIBUTING.md`, which is for agents. Your workspace has no `[version]` table, so:
- **`rung next --ver 0.0.1-0`** is refused: "the config has no `[version] bump` … bump the version by hand and leave --ver out". No rung is marked.
- **A bare `rung next`** works: it only marks the opening `(current)`.
- **`rung commit`** checks no version, because that check needs `[version] file` and `pattern`.

So a project with no version at all runs the whole cycle with no bump and no check. Once you add `Cargo.toml`, an xtask with `bump`, and this to `.vc-config.md`, `--ver` starts working:

```toml
[version]
file = "Cargo.toml"
pattern = 'version = '
bump = "cargo xtask bump {ver}"
```

**Added to rung 1: `cycle --ladder` works before the bookmark exists.** `TODO.md` is the source, so without the bookmark the ladder is made with no rung done. It's still refused when the existing ladder has a rung marked `(done)`, since rebuilding without the cycle's commits would lose those marks; the message points to `--bookmark`.
- There's a new test for this, and the old test that expected a refusal now commits the opening first, so it still covers `--bookmark`.
- The README, the `--ladder` help and rung 1's subsection all describe it.

Full validation passes, and the new `vc-x1-dev` is installed. Rung 1 is still waiting on your review, with this change included.

message.content: When we're done with this cycle here in vc-x1 we won't require --multi-step for  `cycle --close -sb`, correct?

content.text:
Correct. Once this cycle lands, `--multi-step` goes away. The command also changes form, since the stages become subcommands with no compatibility:

```
vc-x1 cycle close -s b                     # the closing commit, linear
vc-x1 cycle close -s b --trapezoid main    # the closing as a merge with main
```

- **Rung 2** turns `cycle --close` into `cycle close`.
- **Rung 3** removes `--single-step`, `--multi-step` and the commit-count check.

After that, `cycle close` always makes a closing commit above the ladder. The other shape comes from a different command:
- A single-step comes from a bare version on the opening, finished by `rung commit`.
- A ladder becomes one commit with `cycle squash` (rung 4).

`cycle close` on a branch with no commit is still refused, since there's no opening for the closing to follow. The message will point to the two ways on: commit the opening first, or use a bare version for a single-step.

I've fixed a single-step `--close` with the opening current. A test covers it, full validation passes, and the dev build is reinstalled.

Your "Single-step test" Todo is the first thing to try in your test workspace:

1. **Single-step after `rung next`**: `cycle --land main -s b` the ladder you just closed. Then `cycle --open --title "feat: single-step test"`, `rung next`, `echo ghi > ghi.txt`, and `cycle --close -sb --single-step --body "..."`. This is the fixed path. Check that the commit's `zTOC.md` reads `0 (done) feat: single-step test`.

Other untested paths, roughly in order of value:

2. **`--ver` that succeeds and one that fails.** The unit test only covers the missing-config refusal. Without a cargo project, a script stands in for the bump:
   - Add `[version]` with `file = "VERSION"`, `pattern = "version = "`, `bump = "./bump.sh {ver}"`.
   - `bump.sh` writes `version = $1` into `VERSION`.
   - `rung next --ver 0.1.0-0` should then run the script and mark the rung. `rung commit` passes the version check.
   - Make the script `exit 1`: the rung should stay unmarked.
   - Leave the version unchanged: `rung commit` is refused, and `--same-version` commits anyway.
3. **`rung stop` mid-rung**: with an edit in `@`, `rung stop` clears the marker and keeps the edit. A following `rung next` re-marks the same rung.
4. **Editing headings while a rung is current**, then `cycle --ladder`:
   - Insert a heading above the current rung: its number shifts and the marker stays.
   - Rename the current rung's heading: the marker is dropped, with a warning.
5. **`cycle --close` with a work rung current**: it should be refused, naming `rung commit` and `rung stop`.
6. **`cycle --status` at each step**: it should name the started rung and how to commit it, or `rung next` and what it starts.
7. **Edge cases**:
   - `--dry-run` on `rung next`, `stop` and `commit` should change nothing.
   - Run from a subdirectory or with `-R`.
   - `rung next` after the cycle has closed should be refused, naming why.

I'd skip a plain-repo `-s p` test. It goes through the same commit code `cycle --commit` already tests.

I agree, and it's a better design than rung 3's. A single-step is one rung of real work, and opening and closing bookends only make sense on a ladder. So the shape should come from `TODO.md`, the gospel, not from the version.

**Proposal for rung 3:**

1. **`cycle --open` scaffolds a single-step**: `#### Rungs` holds one heading, the cycle title itself, and the ladder is `- [feat: single-step test](...)`.
   - `rung next` marks it `(current)`, you do the work, and `rung commit -sb --body` commits it under that title. The record moves to `## Closed`, the ladder becomes `0 (done) feat: single-step test`, and there's no `cycle --close`.
2. **A ladder is planned by adding work rungs**, and then the bookends are needed. `cycle --ladder` writes the `<title> opening` and `<title> closing` headings when the plan has more than the one rung, so you never type bookends.
3. **The version is checked against the shape, not used to choose it.** `rung next --ver` must be bare on a single-step's one rung and on a ladder's closing, and suffixed (`-0`, `-N`) on everything else. A mismatch is refused or warned, not a silent reshape.
4. **`cycle squash` (rung 4) is unchanged.** It turns a ladder into one commit, ending at the same `0 (done) <title>` ladder.

- It's the one commit, so "one title per step" makes the cycle title and commit title identical.
- `git log --grep "<cycle title>"` finds it.

If you want them to differ, the simpler fix is to title the cycle `feat: create ghi.txt` in the first place.

```
cycle plan --title "feat: x"
rung next --ver 1.2.3     # bare version
#   work, validate, review
rung commit --body "..."
```

Your "unnatural" point is about this style, and rung 3 as written only half fixes it. It rewrites the zTOC ladder to one entry but leaves `TODO.md`'s two bookend headings, so the gospel still says opening and closing. I'd make two changes:

2. **`rung next --ver 1.2.3` with a bare version, on a scaffold still holding only its bookends**, rewrites those two headings in `TODO.md` into the one `##### feat: x`, keeping the opening's text. That's the shortcut, and from then on the gospel shows the real rung.

I'd keep `--ver` on `rung next`, not `rung commit`. The bump changes `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`, so it has to come before validation and the review. That's the one place I'd hold the line on "or some such".

One flow for every cycle. `vc-x1 cycle plan` makes the bookmark and scaffolds the record and the
ladder, the version untouched. `vc-x1 rung next --ver <version>` marks the first rung not done
`(current)` in the working copy and bumps the version by the command the config's `[version] bump`
names, and `rung commit` commits it, `(done)` and none current, `rung stop` clearing the marker
instead. A bare version on the opening, however it was set, makes the opening the whole cycle, its
ladder one entry and its `rung commit` the single-step. Otherwise `rung next` reaches the closing
like any rung, and `cycle close` commits it, or `cycle squash` makes the ladder one commit, the
agent commits re-pointed to it. The stages are subcommands, `cycle
plan|close|squash|land|push|status|ladder` and `rung next|stop|commit`, the old flags gone, and the
agent-files say so.
----
  naming `cycle close` and `cycle squash`. `rung next` while a rung is current is refused, and
  `rung stop` clears the marker, the edits left alone.
- A single-step, `cycle plan`, `rung next --ver X.Y.Z`, `rung commit --body`, leaves one commit
  above `main` under the bare title, the record in `## Closed`, and the ladder `0 (done) <title>`.
  So does the same with the version bumped by hand and a bare `rung next`. A bare version on an
  opening whose plan has work rungs is refused.
- A ladder closed by `cycle close --trapezoid main` is a merge of two. Closed by `cycle squash`
----
    `Cargo.lock` after the validate and the review, a tree no one validated.
  - `cycle plan` changes no version: the opening is reached by `rung next`, like every rung.
- **A bare version, however set, makes a single-step** (wink, 2026-11-20): the opening's version
  without a suffix makes the opening the whole cycle, the ladder rewritten to one entry under the
  bare title, and its `rung commit`, its `--body` required, commits it as `cycle --close
  --single-step` did, the record moved to `## Closed`. Under the [suffix
  scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme) a bare version is only ever a cycle's last commit,
  so the version says the shape.
  - However set (wink): `rung next --ver X.Y.Z` is the easy and typical way, and a version bumped by
    hand is read the same, so `rung commit` decides from the version line `[version]` names, and
    `rung next --ver` with a bare version rewrites the ladder early, so the shape shows before the
    review. Without `[version]` there is no version to read, and the single-step is by `cycle
    squash`.

    `X.Y.Z-0`.
  - `--single-step`, `--multi-step`, and the commit-count check go, the shape said by the version
    or by the verb.
- **`cycle squash` makes a ladder one commit** (wink, 2026-11-20): the work rungs squashed into the
  opening, whose change id jj keeps, under the bare title, the record moved to `## Closed` as a
  single-step's.

### feat: the bookmark is made first

(wink + agent, 2026-11-19, split from **feat: one cycle flow, plan, rungs, close** 2026-11-20) A
cycle's bookmark is made by `cycle --open`, which also names it from the title and moves the
title's `## Todo` entry, so a bookmark cannot be made before the title is known, and the habit of a
bookmark first, which keeps a commit or push from reaching a shared line, `main` or a release
branch, has no command of its own. `cycle --status` finds the bookmark by the title's slug alone,
so one named by `--bookmark` is not found. The stage names below are the ones **feat: one cycle
flow, plan, rungs, close** lands, `--open` becoming `cycle plan`.

- **Solution**: `vc-x1 bookmark` with the subcommands `create`, `delete`, `rename`, `move`, and
  `list`, `create` with no name making a provisional `cycle-<ts>`, so a bookmark is the first thing
  made, before any title. `cycle plan` inherits the bookmark it finds on `@`, refusing one that
  tracks a remote, and records its name, which a bare `cycle status` reads. The agent-files say the
  bookmark is made first, provisional while its name is unsettled, and why: no shared line is
  written by accident.
- **Acceptance check**, in a fresh `vc-x1 init` workspace with the cycle's dev build:
  - `vc-x1 bookmark create -s w` makes `cycle-<ts>` on `@`, and `cycle plan --title "<title>"`
    inherits it, writing its name into the record, and a bare `cycle status` names it.
  - `vc-x1 bookmark rename -s w cycle-<ts> <name>` moves the bookmark and the record's name, and a
    bare `cycle status` names `<name>`.
  - `cycle plan` refuses on an `@` carrying two local bookmarks, naming both, and on one carrying a
    bookmark that tracks a remote, `main` moved onto it.
- **Rungs, provisional**: **feat: vc-x1 bookmark and its subcommands**, `delete-bookmark` and
  `move-bookmark` replaced; **feat: cycle plan inherits the bookmark on @**, the record's name read
  by every stage, and the scaffold no longer claiming a `## Todo` entry when there was none;
  **docs: the bookmark is made first**, Opening, Cycles run on a bookmark and its why, jj.md's
  Create, and `cycle-model.md`'s Who writes what.
- **A `bookmark` command, not a provisional `--open`**: making a bookmark is its own command, and
  `cycle plan` inherits it.
  - The state-recording Todo's design, `--open` without `--title`, a `### (untitled)` heading, and a
    later rename, kept the bookmark inside the cycle machinery, so the habit could not run without
    a cycle.
  - It follows jj's `jj bookmark`, so the names are the ones its users know, and it replaces
    `delete-bookmark` and `move-bookmark`.
- **A generated name is renamed by hand alone**: `create` with no name makes `cycle-<ts>`, `<ts>`
  UTC to the second in ISO 8601's basic form, and nothing renames it automatically.
  - The tool never renames a bookmark on its own, so no stage's output depends on whether a name
    was given or generated, and the record needs no `provisional` flag.
  - The cost accepted: a forgotten `cycle-<ts>` keeps its name until someone renames it.
  - `cycle plan` without an inherited bookmark or `--bookmark` makes `cycle-<ts>` too, or the
    title's slug as today, to be decided (wink suggested `cycle-<ts>`, 2026-11-20).
- **`rename` rewrites the record**: renaming the cycle's own bookmark rewrites the name the record
  holds, so a bare `cycle status` still finds it. `bookmark` knows the record for that one name
  and nothing else.
- **`rename` and `delete` of a pushed bookmark push**: free while local, and with an `origin`
  bookmark each is a push and takes approval.
- **No `set`**: jj's `set` is create or move, which is the move of a shared line the habit guards
  against. `list` is cheap and pairs with the `status` and `list` cleanup.
- **Scope**: `-s w` and `-s p`, `a` and `b` refused, since the agent-repo is a linear journal and
  carries no bookmark.
- **What `cycle plan` inherits**:
  - With `--bookmark <NAME>`, that bookmark when it is on `@`, else it is created.
  - Without it, the one local bookmark on `@`, a new one made when there is none, and refused
    over two or more, naming each.
  - Never a bookmark that tracks a remote, so a trunk moved onto `@` is refused rather than adopted.
- **The record holds the bookmark**: a `toml` block under the `###` cycle heading, `bookmark =
  "<name>"`, a subset of the state-recording Todo's cycle block, which that cycle extends rather
  than replaces.
- **No `--retitle` and no `(untitled)`**: with the bookmark made first, `cycle plan` runs once the
  title is known, so neither is needed.

### feat: status and list print @ and @- alike

(wink + agent, 2026-11-19, split from **feat: one cycle flow, plan, rungs, close** 2026-11-20)
`vc-x1 status` and `vc-x1 list` print the same commit differently, `status` the change and commit
ids and `list` the change id and ochid, at different lengths, and `list` reads `.` without `-s`
where `status` reads the work-repo, so neither confirms what the other shows. Likely a single-step
cycle.

- **Solution**: one commit line, the change id, commit id, ochid, bookmarks, and description, made
  by one formatter both commands call. `vc-x1 status` prints each repo's lines as `jj st` does, its
  short ids and spacing, its per-repo labels and verdict line kept. `vc-x1 list` prints as `jj log`
  does, the graph, author, and timestamp added, one section per repo under `-s b`. Both default
  `-s` to `work`, found by the workspace, and `list`'s `-n` to 2, so a bare `list` shows the `@`
  and `@-` a bare `status` shows.
- **Acceptance check**, in a fresh `vc-x1 init` workspace with the cycle's dev build:
  - `vc-x1 status -s w` and `jj st` print the same lines for the repo, and `vc-x1 list -s w -r
    <revset>` and `jj log -r <revset>` the same lines, each commit line with its ochid added after
    the commit id.
  - From the workspace root and from a subdirectory, a bare `vc-x1 list` shows the work-repo's `@`
    and `@-`, the two commits a bare `vc-x1 status` shows.
- **`status` and `list` agree**: both default `-s` to `work`, and a bare `list` shows `@` and `@-`,
  `-n 2`, the commits `status` shows. Their other options and the other commands' are left for
  later cycles.
- **Both show three ids**: each commit's change id, commit id, and ochid, jj's two and vc-x1's
  pairing, the ochid empty on an uncommitted `@`.
  - jj's two alone would drop the pairing, the one thing vc-x1 adds to a dual repo, and the change
    id and ochid alone would drop the commit id `jj st` shows.
- **One title** (wink, 2026-11-19): "print @ and @- alike", the point being consistency between
  the two commands, not likeness to jj.
