  It is committed by `vc-x1-dev rung commit -s b --body "..."`, and the next rung started by
  `vc-x1-dev rung next --ver 0.85.26-3`.

  `0.85.25` has no `rung` and no stage subcommands, and writes the next rung `(current)` into a
  commit. The bookmark is the title's slug, so no `--bookmark` is needed.''')
r('''flags go, and the rehearsal, README, and tests name the subcommands.

- `cycle` is a command with subcommands, `plan`, `ladder`, `status`, `close`, `land`, and `push`,
  each with its own arguments, so a flag another stage owns is clap's "unexpected argument" and the
  "takes no" refusals went. `Where`, the bookmark, `-R`, and `--dry-run`, is shared with `rung`'s
  acts, and `-s` is required by clap on `close`, `land`, and `push`.
- `cycle --commit` is gone, `rung commit` being the one way a rung is committed, and `rung_params`
  builds a rung's commit for `rung commit` and `cycle close` alike. The tests commit a rung by that
  code with a title given, so the title refusals stay tested.
- A stage's target is positional, `cycle land <TARGET>` and `cycle close [REV,...]`'s heads. `close
  --land <TARGET>` chains the Land, `--skip` and `--delete-intermediate-bookmarks` requiring it,
  and `land`'s `--title` and `--body` require `--merge`. `-s w` on `land` and `push` is refused by
  one message.
- Every message names the subcommand, `cycle plan`, `cycle close`, and `rung commit` where it said
  `cycle --open`, `--close`, and `--commit`. `cycle -h` lists the stages, and each stage's long help
  is its own.
- The rehearsal starts and commits the opening and each rung by `rung next` and `rung commit`,
  checks the marker `rung next` writes, and tries `rung commit` with no rung started where it tried
  an unplanned title. README's `### cycle` shows the subcommands, the commit's details moved to `###
  rung`, and `vc-config.md`'s `used-by` names them. The agent-files still name the flags until the
  docs rung.
''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

I've finished rung 2 (**feat: cycle stages are subcommands**, version 0.85.26-2) and it's ready for your review. Full validation passes, the rehearsal passes 50/50 and the dev build is reinstalled from the working copy.

**What changed:**
- **The stage flags are now subcommands:** `cycle plan`, `ladder`, `status`, `close`, `land` and `push`. There is no compatibility, so `cycle --open` is now just a clap error.
  - `cycle land <TARGET>` and `cycle close [REV,...]` take their target and heads as positional arguments.
  - A later stage still chains as a flag: `cycle close -s b --multi-step --land main --push`.
  - `-s` is required on `close`, `land` and `push`.
  - `land`'s `--title` and `--body` work only with `--merge`.
- **`cycle --commit` is gone:** `rung commit` is the only way to commit a rung. It and `cycle close` now share the commit-building code. The tests still pass a title straight to that code, so the title refusals stay tested.
- **Messages and help name the subcommands** throughout (`cycle plan`, `cycle close`, `rung commit`). `cycle -h` lists the stages, and each stage has its own long help.
- **Rehearsal:** it now runs the opening and each rung with `rung next` / `rung commit` and checks the `(current)` marker (two new checks). Where it used to try a commit with an unplanned title, it now tries `rung commit` with no rung started, and the tool refuses it.
- **README:** `### cycle` shows the subcommands, and the commit details moved under `### rung`.
- **Other files:** `vc-config.md`'s `used-by` lines are updated, and TODO.md has rung 2's subsection and refreshed continuation notes.

The agent-files (AGENTS.md, jj.md, cycle-model.md and others) still describe the old flags. The ladder leaves them to rung 5, `docs: one cycle flow`, so until then they describe commands that no longer exist.

# Commit model

Two commit bodies from the `config loader` cycle in [cycle-model.md](cycle-model.md), shown as
specimens rather than a skeleton: a work rung's body and a bookend's. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [Commit-body form](prose.md#commit-body-form).

## A work rung

Title: `refactor: split loader from parser`

```
Config loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load a
config without parsing it and a test cannot parse one without a file on
disk. The move into its own module is what forces the split.

Solution: a loader finds and reads the file and a parser takes text and
returns the schema, so a test hands the parser a string, and `main` gets
the schema from one call.

See details in TODO.md:
##### refactor: split loader from parser
```

The first paragraph states this commit's problem and defines "split", the word the title assumes.
The second opens "Solution:", nothing names a file that the diff already lists, and the pointer
is the rung's subsection heading, a line of its own, which a search of `TODO.md` finds at any
commit.

## A bookend

Title: `refactor: extract config loader opening`

```
Opens the cycle "refactor: extract config loader".

See details in TODO.md:
### refactor: extract config loader
```

A bookend resolves no problem of its own, so its body names the cycle by its title and points at
its record, the cycle's heading. The closing's body is the same shape with "Closes".

`#### Rungs` holds the **rung subsections**, one per rung in the ladder's order, the closing
included, headed by the rung's exact title, so the ladder is their index. Each opens at laddering
with an abstract-sized intent statement (the rung's problem and solution in a sentence or two) and
completes at the rung's landing with the conceptual delta: design points, consequences, deferrals,
never a restatement of the landed commit body. The closing rung's opens with the stub "Closing out
the cycle." and completes at close-out with what closing taught, in problem/solution form, or
`_None._`.

A rung is `- N (marker) [<title>](TODO.md#<slug>)` and carries no detail beyond that: the title
links to the rung's subsection. A step is identified by its title (prose.md's [Steps are named, not
numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)), so a title carries no number, no version, and no
SHA. The version-of-record still bumps for every rung and its suffix still encodes the stage, but
that encoding belongs to the manifest and appears nowhere in prose.

A single-step cycle's ladder is one unlinked rung, `- N (marker) <cycle title>`, with no subsection
under it: a subsection headed by the title would collide with the title heading's anchor ([Cycle
shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).

The block is the cycle's only record. A design finding that must outlive the cycle goes into a
`notes/` file by the rung that made it ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).

## zTOC format

`zTOC.md`, beside `TODO.md` at the work-repo root, is the workspace's index, so the running ladder
and the files worth knowing are found without reading `TODO.md`'s length, and the `z` sorts it last
in a listing. Its sections, in this order:

- `# TOC`, the title.
- `## Ladder`: the cycle's ladder, its one copy, each rung with its marker as [The In Progress
  block](#the-in-progress-block) shapes it, linking across to its subsection in `TODO.md`, since a
  same-file link does not work in every markdown preview, zed's among them. Written by `vc-x1
  cycle --open`, replacing the last cycle's, made again from the rung headings by `cycle --ladder`
  and by every cycle commit, and kept by the closing commit, so the landmark's tree holds the
  finished ladder beside its `## Closed`. Its grammar is strict: each rung a left-margin `- `
  line, and the tool refuses to rewrite a ladder holding any other line but a blank one.
- `## The TOC`: one link per file worth knowing, with what it holds, `TODO.md` first, its line
  linking the todo list as well, `[todo list](TODO.md#todo)`, so the Todos are one step away.

Its links are inline, so it has no `# References`.

Like `TODO.md` it is not an agent-file, and `scripts/vc-dr-apply.sh` ships it as a skeleton, `##
Ladder` reading `_None._` until the first opening.

cycle-record became `TODO.md > ## In Progress` alone ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).

numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)), so a title carries no number, no version, and no
SHA. The version-of-record still bumps for every rung and its suffix still encodes the stage, but
that encoding belongs to the manifest and appears nowhere in prose.

A single-step cycle's ladder is one unlinked rung, `- N (marker) <cycle title>`, with no subsection
under it: a subsection headed by the title would collide with the title heading's anchor ([Cycle
shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).

The block is the cycle's only record. A design finding that must outlive the cycle goes into a
`notes/` file by the rung that made it ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).

## zTOC format

`zTOC.md`, beside `TODO.md` at the work-repo root, is the workspace's index, so the running ladder
and the files worth knowing are found without reading `TODO.md`'s length, and the `z` sorts it last
in a listing. Its sections, in this order:

- `# TOC`, the title.
- `## Ladder`: the cycle's ladder, its one copy, each rung with its marker as [The In Progress
  block](#the-in-progress-block) shapes it, linking across to its subsection in `TODO.md`, since a
  same-file link does not work in every markdown preview, zed's among them. Written by `vc-x1
  cycle --open`, replacing the last cycle's, made again from the rung headings by `cycle --ladder`
  and by every cycle commit, and kept by the closing commit, so the landmark's tree holds the
  finished ladder beside its `## Closed`. Its grammar is strict: each rung a left-margin `- `
  line, and the tool refuses to rewrite a ladder holding any other line but a blank one.
- `## The TOC`: one link per file worth knowing, with what it holds, `TODO.md` first, its line
  linking the todo list as well, `[todo list](TODO.md#todo)`, so the Todos are one step away.

Its links are inline, so it has no `# References`.

Like `TODO.md` it is not an agent-file, and `scripts/vc-dr-apply.sh` ships it as a skeleton, `##
Ladder` reading `_None._` until the first opening.

## Frozen history: chores and done

`notes/chores/chores-NN.md` and `notes/done.md` are the records of cycles that ran before the
cycle-record became `TODO.md > ## In Progress` alone ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).

content.text:
I agree a fresh workspace should start with the two files, but there's a catch with putting them in `init`.

**The catch:** `scripts/vc-dr-apply.sh` is run on top of an `init` workspace, and it refuses when any file it ships already exists with different content (lines 5 and 57). It ships its own `TODO.md` and `zTOC.md`, which have agent-data links and a "Configure this workspace" Todo. If `init` writes skeletons, applying the agent-files to a fresh workspace stops working.

**Ways around it:**
1. **Keep it in `cycle plan` (rung 3 as it stands).** `init` stays bare, `vc-dr-apply` still works, and the files appear on the first plan. The cost is that you can't add a Todo entry before the first plan unless you create `TODO.md` yourself.
2. **`init` writes them, and `vc-dr-apply` overwrites a file that exactly matches `init`'s skeleton.** This gives your flow (init, write a Todo, plan) and keeps the apply working. It's a bit more work, and the script then has to know `init`'s skeleton text.
3. **Both:** `init` writes them as in option 2, and `cycle plan` keeps its fallback for workspaces made before this change.

I'd go with option 3. Your order (Todo, then plan) is the natural one, and the fallback is already built and tested.

**Picking the Todo to plan.** Today `cycle plan --title X` moves the `## Todo` entry titled X into the record, or writes an empty scaffold if no entry has that title. A natural extension is that a bare `cycle plan` takes the top `## Todo` entry, since that list is in priority order.

That changes how `plan` chooses its input, and the `## Todo` entry **feat: the bookmark is made first** already reworks what `plan` inherits (bookmark, record name). So I'd add "a bare `plan` takes the top Todo" to that entry rather than to this cycle.

If you agree, rung 3 becomes **feat: init writes the record's files**:
- `init` writes the skeletons in its initial commit, the dual and plain-repo modes alike.
- `vc-dr-apply` replaces a file identical to `init`'s skeleton.
- `cycle plan` keeps its fallback.

Should I go that way, or would you rather keep rung 3 as it is (option 1)?

content.text:
Yes, that makes sense: `vc-dr-apply` stops being the way a workspace gets its files, and `init` takes over that job. Here's how I read it:

- **Every new dual repo gets `TODO.md` and `zTOC.md` from `init`**, in its initial commit, whatever else is copied. "Empty" would mean headings only: `## Continuation notes`, `## In Progress`, `## Todo` and `## Closed` in `TODO.md`, and `## Ladder` in `zTOC.md`. That's the skeleton rung 3 already has. Truly empty files wouldn't work, because `cycle plan` needs those headings to write the record.
- **`init` takes a path for the other files** `vc-dr-apply` copies today: the agent-files, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `notes/` and so on. A `TODO.md` or `zTOC.md` in that path would be skipped, so the new repo always starts with the skeletons.

I'd split it:
- **Rung 3 becomes feat: init writes the record's files.** `init` writes the two skeletons in the dual and plain-repo modes alike. `cycle plan` keeps its fallback for workspaces made before this change. It's small and mostly built already.
- **The path option goes into a new `## Todo` entry.** Something like **feat: init copies a set of files**, which replaces `vc-dr-apply`. It needs its own design: what the path holds, the per-language extras (`vc-dr-apply-lang`), the `.gitignore` lines, the agent-side files, and what becomes of the script.

That `## Todo` entry would also hold the earlier idea that a bare `cycle plan` takes the top `## Todo` entry, unless you'd rather keep that with **feat: the bookmark is made first**.

Shall I retitle rung 3 and file the Todo that way?

| `--push-retries <N>` | Max push retries after repo creation [default: 5] |
| `--push-retry-delay <N>` | Seconds between push retries [default: 3] |
| `--config <none\|PATH>` | Override the canned config write, under the name the source's carrier calls for |

init makes a bare workspace, the repos with only `.vc-config.md` and `.gitignore` in them, and what
goes in it is applied afterwards. `--use-template`, which copied template directories in, is gone.

**`--adopt`**. Without it an existing TARGET is refused, named by what it holds. With it, init
grows the target into a dual workspace:

- A plain directory, no repo: both repos are created around it, and everything in it that its
  `.gitignore` does not exclude is the work repo's first commit, whatever the file sizes. Files
  over jj's new-file size limit (1MiB by default) are listed, since jj would otherwise leave them
  out. A `.gitignore` it already has is kept and given the lines it lacks, the agent directory's
  and `/.claude/settings.local.json`.
- A repo, jj colocated with git or git alone, with no workspace config: a git-only repo is
  colocated with jj first, its history kept. Its history stays, and one commit,
  "Adopt as a dual-repo workspace", goes on top, carrying `.vc-config.md`, the `.gitignore` lines,
  and the `ochid:` trailer to the agent repo's first commit. With an `origin`, the agent repo's
  remote is derived beside it, `--repo` and `--account` are refused, and the work side pushes
  nothing: the commit is yours to land. An agent remote init cannot create, one on a host other
  than GitHub, must exist, and is checked before anything is written. With no origin, the remotes
  come from `--repo` as for a fresh init, and both are pushed. A working copy with uncommitted work
writes and push in one shot.

`--repo local=<PARENT>` lays out:
```
<PARENT>/
  remote-work.git/     bare git remote for the work repo
  remote-bot.git/   bare git remote for the .claude bot repo
  <NAME>/              work repo (jj colocated, main tracks origin)
    .vc-config.md      work=".", agent=".claude"
    .gitignore         /target /.claude /.git /.jj /.claude/settings.local.json
    .claude/           bot repo (jj colocated, main tracks origin)
      .vc-config.md    work="..", agent="."
      .gitignore       .git .jj /settings.local.json
```

session was already started in, as `../help` was. Tried by dry run on `../help`, where

none of what would stop it:

  bends "Every argument is a flag" (`jj.md`'s vc-x1 commit and push, and `v0.3.1`'s scope-flags
  change), so the rule names it, or the rule changes to let a command's one required argument be
  positional.

  `~/.claude/projects/<mangled-path>` a real directory, holding its transcript and `memory/`, and
  the symlink step refuses a path that "exists and is not a symlink", the last step, after the
  push. Preflight refuses it with nothing made, or init moves the directory's transcripts into the
  new agent-repo and replaces it with the symlink, the session first exited.

  there leaves it, or the refusal names `--adopt`.

  `/.claude/settings.local.json`, so an adopted `.claude/.cc-writes/` is committed and pushed. The
  wider rule is **Every repo's .gitignore ignores .claude, and settings stay out of agent-repos**,
  and this needs at least the adopted directory's `.claude/` kept out.

  **Initialization leaves no bad link**, init copying no agent-files.

### Initialization leaves no bad link

(wink + agent, 2026-11-16, from **docs: CONTRIBUTING.md names the project's tasks**) A workspace an
initialization makes should have no bad link, and where one cannot be avoided it says what fixes
it, never leaving the reader a broken link to find. The information a link points at travels with
the agent-files, so the fix is to ship it, not to drop the link.

- **One mechanism** (wink, 2026-11-16). Three set a workspace up today: `vc-x1 init`, `--adopt`
  included, makes the repos and copies no agent-files, `scripts/vc-dr-apply.sh` copies the set,
  the base skeleton, and a language skeleton, and `vc-x1 agent-files copy` copies the set between
  adopters. Two ways to start a workspace is acceptable for now, and not for long: `init` takes
  on what `vc-dr-apply` does and the script retires. Whether `agent-files copy` folds in too is
  settled then.
  - Its building blocks (wink + agent, 2026-11-18): `vc-x1 agent-files copy --from` and `vc-x1
    xtask copy --from` each work in a repo fresh from `init`, the second making it a workspace of
    xtask alone, so `init --from DIR` is those two and the base skeleton, `TODO.md`, `zTOC.md`,
    `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `notes/`, and `LICENSE-*`, with the agent repo's `README.md` and
  an unplanned title. README's `### cycle` shows the subcommands, the commit's details moved to `###
  rung`, and `vc-config.md`'s `used-by` names them. The agent-files still name the flags until the
  docs rung.

##### feat: cycle plan writes a missing record

`cycle plan` writes `TODO.md` or `zTOC.md` when the workspace has none, a skeleton of the
headings the record needs, `## In Progress`, `## Todo`, and `## Closed` in `TODO.md` and `##
Ladder` in `zTOC.md`, then the record as it does now, so a bare `vc-x1 init` workspace plans a
cycle with no file made by hand. `--no-record` still writes nothing. Found by wink's test of
rung 2 in a fresh `init` workspace (wink, 2026-11-21).

- `plan_open` reads a missing file as its skeleton, `TODO_SKELETON` or `LADDER_SKELETON`, and
  plans the record on it as on any file, so the skeleton's write and the record's are one edit
  and a refusal or a dry run writes neither. What it did names the skeleton written.
- The skeletons hold the headings alone: `TODO.md`'s `## Continuation notes` reading `_None._`,
  `## In Progress` reading `_No cycle currently in progress._`, and `## Todo` and `## Closed`
  empty, so no placeholder is left when a cycle fills them, and `zTOC.md`'s `## Ladder` reading
  `_None._`. No link into `agent-data/`, which a workspace without the agent-files would not have.
- A file there is kept, the other made, and the refusal that named the two files went, with its
  test, the test now planning a cycle in a workspace with neither and with one.

next` marks it current, and `rung commit --body` commits it under the bare title, the record moved
to `## Closed` without `#### Rungs` and the ladder `0 (done) <title>`. `rung next --ver X.Y.Z`, a

`CONTRIBUTING.md`, `notes/`, and `LICENSE-*`, with the agent repo's `README.md` and
    `memory/MEMORY.md`, which only the script writes today. A flag on either copy for the other
    was set aside: each set has its own version, `diff`, and update, and the one command belongs
    to `init`. `xtask copy` is the first of the script's jobs moved into Rust, `--lang rust`
    calling it, from **feat: the project's tasks move to cargo xtask**.
- The manifest moved into `agent-files(proposal): v0.3.1` (wink, 2026-11-18): the set declared
  as data with set, starter, and optional kinds, the starters being the skeleton below, so this
  entry keeps `init --from DIR` on top of it, the script's retirement, and the cross-file link
  check.
- **The skeleton is part of the agent-files.** `TODO.md`, `zTOC.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and
  `notes/`'s `README.md`, `bugs.md`, and `todo-backlog.md` are required and shaped by the
  agent-files, their content each project's, and they live in `scripts/vc-dr-apply-base/` beside
  the script. They move into the set's tree, named as required with their shape, so a copy of the
  agent-files carries what their links point at, and `agent-files diff` checks the shape, not
  the content.
- **Links are checked across files.** `vc-x1 validate-anchors` checks a file's links to itself and
  skips the rest. It learns to follow a link into another file and to its anchor, and an
  initialization runs it on what it made. A link it cannot satisfy, `custom.md`'s, local and
  gitignored, for one, is reported with what fixes it.
  - The rung's hand check, a script, found 40 bad cross-file links of 646 in vc-x1's own tree. The
    starter files' 14 are relative to the workspace they are written into, so bad only where they
    sit. The frozen history's 15, `notes/done.md` and `notes/chores/`, retire under **Retire the
    frozen history**. The live 11 are anchors renamed since: `README.md:2500` and
    `notes/todo-backlog.md:54`'s `#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push`, `TODO.md`'s
    `jj.md#vc-x1-push-what-it-does-and-does-not-do`, and the rest in `notes/todo-backlog.md`,
    `notes/refactor-20260716.md`, `notes/transcript-format.md`, and
    `notes/design-cli/por-dual-parity-audit.md`. The script's slug is GitHub's rule by hand, so a
    few may be its own mistake.
- **The language skeletons are too narrow.** `--lang NAME` offers four, wink has used none, every
  project so far Rust and a test or toy, and what a real project starts from is likely more than a
  directory of files: cloning a template repo, or a project's own skeleton. Open, to be settled
  when a real project needs it.

### Durable messaging between projects

That's a list of paths stored with the agent-files themselves (a TOML block in `AGENTS.md` or an `agent-data/set.toml`), and each entry has one of three kinds:
- **set:** kept identical to the source and replaced on copy, like `AGENTS.md` and `agent-data/`.
- **starter:** written only when absent, like `TODO.md`, `zTOC.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `notes/`.
- **optional:** copied only when asked, like `custom.md`.

A project's own config may only narrow that list.

I'd keep that over a table in `.vc-config.md`, for two reasons:
- The list describes the set, so it should travel with it. `.vc-config.md` describes one workspace and is written fresh for each, not copied. Its table would make sense as the narrowing layer (files to skip).
- It already fits your decision: starters are written only when absent, so the `TODO.md` and `zTOC.md` that `init` writes stay.

I've noted this as an open question, with your suggestion and my view, under **Initialization leaves no bad link**. - **`cycle plan`** keeps writing the skeleton into workspaces made before this change.
- **Tests:** the plain-repo `init` test checks both skeletons are committed, and the adopt test checks an existing `TODO.md` is kept while `zTOC.md` is written. The cycle tests that need a workspace without the files now delete `init`'s copies first.
- **Docs:** README (the `init` and `plan` sections), the code comments and the rung's subsection are updated.

Full validation passes, the rehearsal passes 50/50, and the dev build is reinstalled from the working copy. Your `vc-x1-dev init --test-repo ...` then `cycle plan --title ...` sequence should now work with no hand-made files.

content.content:
- Any other commit is a work rung, under its heading under `#### Rungs`, which gives `--body`, the
  text or `@PATH`.
- The ladder is rewritten first, the rung done and none current, so `zTOC.md` at the commit
  shows the cycle as of it, and it is put back when the commit is not made.
- The cycle's bookmark is the one advanced, the slug of the title in `## In Progress` or
  `--bookmark`'s, so no other bookmark on the line moves.

`-s` is required: `b` makes the pair, `w` the work half with the agent half left to `push`, and
`p` a plain repo's commit. A scope the workspace does not fit, `p` in a dual workspace or `b` in a
plain repo, is refused. `--push` publishes the rung on the cycle's bookmark, a draft push. Refused
before the ladder is written: a rung committed already, which [`squash`](#squash) continues, an
empty work `@`, and a work rung with no body. `--dry-run` prints the descriptions and commits
nothing.

`cycle close` is refused while a rung other than the closing is current, so a rung is never
left in flight. `--bookmark` names the cycle's bookmark when it is not the title's slug, and `-R`
says where.

### trailers

Rewrite a range of work commits' trailers to what is stamped today ([Cross-repo
Linking](#cross-repo-linking-with-git-trailers)), only their descriptions changing, each tree checked
unchanged. It is how a cycle or a test repo moves to a new protocol, and a Land runs the same pass.

My take: `cycle plan` doesn't need file-set. It only needs `TODO.md` and `zTOC.md` with their headings. Rung 3, now committed, gives it those two ways: `init` writes the skeletons, and `plan` writes them itself if they're missing. File-set covers everything else (the agent-files, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `notes/`), and none of those are read by `plan`.

The dependency actually runs the other way. File-set builds on this cycle:
- `init --from DIR` copies starters only when absent, so it relies on rung 3's skeletons already being there.
- The manifest names its files by kind, so it's simplest to design once `TODO.md` and `zTOC.md` are settled as `init`'s own.

Running it before this cycle isn't practical now anyway. This cycle has three rungs committed locally plus rung 4 in review. Parking it, landing file-set on `main` and rebasing this cycle back on top would mean conflicts in `init.rs` and `TODO.md`, and the version numbers would need reworking.

- **Finish this cycle as planned.** That's rung 4, `cycle squash`, the docs rung, and the closing.

content.text:
Two quick checks before I write anything.

**1. "file-set.toml".** I'm not sure which change you mean:
- (a) The manifest lives at `file-set.toml` in the set's root, so `init --from DIR` reads `DIR/file-set.toml` instead of `DIR/agent-data/file-set.toml`.
- (b) The Todo is titled after it, e.g. **feat: init copies by file-set.toml**, instead of **feat: init copies a file set**.
- (c) Something else.

**2. Picking the Todo in `cycle plan`.** I like this. It's a fuller form of the "a bare `cycle plan` takes the top Todo" idea now in **feat: the bookmark is made first**. Here's how I'd shape it:
- **The argument:** `cycle plan [TODO]`, an optional positional argument naming a `## Todo` entry.
- **A number** is an offset into `## Todo`: `1` is the top entry, `2` the next, and so on.
- **Anything else** is a sequence of consecutive words in the title, matched whole-word and ignoring case. So `cycle plan "squash refuses"` finds **feat: squash-push refuses an agent push that names unpublished work**.
- **The match must be unique.** Zero matches or more than one are refused, listing the candidates with their offsets so the next try can use a number.
- **The title** comes from the entry's heading, so `--title` isn't needed. `--title` stays for a cycle with no entry (the empty scaffold) and can't be combined with `TODO`.
- **A bare `cycle plan`:** I'd keep it refused rather than defaulting to `1`, so a cycle is never planned by accident. Or should bare mean `1`?

**3. Where it goes.** It's about `cycle plan`, which fits this cycle's subject. It could be a rung here, inserted after rung 4, or recorded in **feat: the bookmark is made first**, which already reworks what `plan` inherits. Which do you prefer?

Rung 4 is still waiting for your review.

content.text:
I've recorded both decisions in TODO.md.

**`file-set.toml` lives at the set's root.** By default `init --from DIR` reads `DIR/file-set.toml`, not `DIR/agent-data/file-set.toml`, and `--file-set PATH` names a different one. I changed this in **feat: init copies a file set** and in the manifest bullet of **agent-files(proposal): v0.3.1**.

**`cycle plan [TODO]` picks the Todo to plan.** This replaced the old "a bare `cycle plan` takes the top Todo" bullet in **feat: the bookmark is made first**:
- **No argument:** the top `## Todo` entry.
- **A number:** an offset, `1` being the top.
- **Anything else:** consecutive words from a title, matched whole-word and ignoring case. Zero matches or more than one are refused, listing the candidates with their offsets.
- **Confirmation:** each form asks you to confirm the entry's title unless `--yes` is given. I only pass `--yes` with your approval, as with `push --yes`. With no terminal and no `--yes` it's refused, and nothing is made.
- **`--title`** stays for a cycle with no Todo entry, and is refused alongside `TODO`.

While editing, I also rewrapped a few lines I had touched in those entries that ran past 100 characters. These are record edits only, carried in rung 4's working copy, and fast validation passes.

Rung 4, **feat: a single-step is one rung**, is still waiting for your review.

content.text:
I'd hold off on a stored index. For the tool, there's nothing slow to save:
- `TODO.md` is 5,178 lines (358 KB). Scanning it for `## Todo` headings takes about a millisecond.
- `vc-x1-dev cycle ladder --dry-run` takes 53 ms end to end, and `cycle status` 138 ms. Nearly all of that is process start-up and the jj calls, not reading `TODO.md`.
- A cache keyed on the file's modification time would add a file to keep in sync, and checkout or rewrite can change that time without changing the content. It would cost more than it saves.

Where it does cost is me reading it. All of `TODO.md` is roughly 90k tokens, which is why the acquaint reads only a slice and `zTOC.md` holds the ladder. A computed index fixes that without storing anything: a command that prints the `## Todo` entries with their offsets, for example:

```
$ vc-x1 cycle plan --list      # or a `vc-x1 todo list`
1  feat: init copies a file set
2  feat: the bookmark is made first
3  feat: status and list print @ and @- alike

content.text:
Numbered, with `-n` for the count, sounds right: `-n` is already the count on `list`, `status` and `check desc` (where its long form is `--commits`). For the starting number I'd avoid `-s`, though:
- `-s` means scope on 18 commands. Your hands, and mine, will type `-s b` out of habit, and in `todo list` that would quietly mean "start at b" or fail with a confusing message.
- A command with no scope today may get one later. If `todo list` ever reads a Todo from another workspace, `-s` would be needed for scope.

I'd make the starting number long-only, `--start N`, the rarer of the two options. Positional (`todo list 10`) would read nicely, but the project rule is that every argument is a flag, and the `init <TARGET>` Todo is already arguing for one exception.

```
vc-x1 todo list                 # every entry, numbered from 1
vc-x1 todo list -n 10           # the top ten
vc-x1 todo list --start 11 -n 10  # the next ten
```

- **Numbers are offsets into `## Todo`**, 1-based, the same numbers `cycle plan` takes. `--start 11` lists from the 11th entry and keeps its number, so the number shown is still the one you pass.
- **Default:** every entry. There are 155 today, about 3k tokens, fine for a terminal or for me, and `-n` trims it.
- **No `-s`:** it reads the work-repo's `TODO.md`, and `-R` says which workspace, as on the other commands.
- **Out of range:** `--start` past the end prints nothing and says so; it isn't an error.

Should I record it that way, or would you rather keep `-s` for start?

I think it should work too. It's the simple single-step at its shortest, with no plan step:

```
echo abc > abc.txt
vc-x1 rung commit -s b --title "feat: create abc" --body '...'
```

**What it would do** when no cycle is in progress and `--title` is given:
1. Plan the cycle as `cycle plan --title` would: make the bookmark on `@` (the title's slug), and write the record with the one heading, the title. If a `## Todo` entry has that title, its text moves into the record as usual.
2. Commit it as the cycle's one commit, the same commit rung 4 makes: bare title, record moved to `## Closed`, ladder `0 (done) feat: create abc`.
3. Leave it on the bookmark, so `cycle land main -s b --push` lands it. `main` still only moves at the Land.

**Things to settle:**
- **The record's text.** The scaffold would otherwise close with Problem and Solution reading `_To write._`. I'd fill them from the body: its first paragraph as the Problem, its `Solution:` paragraph as the Solution, and the rest `_None._`. The record then says what the commit says.
- **The version.** With `[version]` in the config, the commit is refused if the version is unchanged. You either bump by hand first, or `rung commit` takes `--ver`. We moved `--ver` to `rung next` so the bump is reviewed. Here nothing comes between, though `@` is still in front of you before you commit, so I'd allow `--ver` on this form only. Your test workspace has no `[version]`, so it doesn't arise there.
- **With a cycle already in progress,** `--title` stays refused, since the rung's title comes from the ladder.
- **Which command.** `rung commit` reads naturally: the whole cycle is one rung. Today's `vc-x1 commit -s b --title --body` would also accept it, but it advances `main` locally, which is the habit the bookmark protects against.

**Two notes on your run:**
- **The backticks ran.** Inside double quotes the shell ran `echo abc > abc.txt` as a command substitution, so the body lost that text and `abc.txt` was rewritten. Single quotes keep it literal: `--body 'Created abc.txt with `echo abc > abc.txt`'`.
- **`-s` is required.** The next refusal would have been the missing `-s b`. Whether `-s b` should become the default is still open from earlier.

**Where it goes:** I'd insert it as its own rung after rung 4, **feat: rung commit plans a single-step**, so rung 4 is reviewed as it stands. Folding it into rung 4 is the alternative, since it's the same story. Which do you prefer? And is filling the record from the body right?

**The verbatim form**, when no cycle is in progress:

```
echo abc > abc.txt
vc-x1 rung commit -s b --title "feat: create abc" --body '...'
vc-x1 cycle land main -s b --push
```

- It makes the bookmark on `@`, the title's slug or `--bookmark`'s, refused if that name is already in use. Then it commits the pair exactly as given, title and body as written, the bookmark advanced and `main` untouched.
- It leaves `TODO.md` and `zTOC.md` alone and doesn't need them to exist.

**The automated form** takes a flag, e.g. `--record`:
- It plans the cycle with the one heading, as `cycle plan --title` would, moving a matching `## Todo` entry in.
- It fills the record's Problem and Solution from the body.
- It closes the cycle in the same commit: record in `## Closed`, ladder `0 (done) <title>`.

**How it differs from `vc-x1 commit -s b --title --body`:** that one advances the nearest bookmark below `@`, which is `main` in a fresh workspace. This one always works on a cycle bookmark, so the habit that `main` only moves at the Land holds.

content.content:
### Improve init and add rename and delete subcommands

(wink + agent, 2026-10-11) A workspace's name is written into six places, and nothing renames or
removes them together: the work-repo's directory, the agent-repo's directory when it is not
nested, the two repos on the remote, each repo's `origin` URL, the `.vc-config.{toml|md}` of both
sides, and the Claude Code symlink. And `init` makes a workspace it cannot always finish, or that
Claude Code does not find.

- The order is wink's: `init` is fixed first, then `vc-x1 delete`, then `vc-x1 rename`. Each is a
  cycle of its own.
- The `init` work is more than one cycle, wink's order: the path over 200 characters, then the
  name GitHub would change, the order the two parts below are in. The first part, the agent
  template `--use-template` looked for, retired with the flag (2026-11-03).
- Delete is ahead of rename: its "find every part of a workspace from its config" is what rename
  reuses, and it gives `init` the cleanup it lacks.
- The parts are `####` headings, where [Todo format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format) asks for
  bullets with a bold title, since a heading is an anchor a link can name.
- Delete leans on two entries far down this list: the clean verdict of [status prints a verdict
  per repo and exits with a bit per
  side](#status-prints-a-verdict-per-repo-and-exits-with-a-bit-per-side), and [status reports the
  commits no bookmark reaches](#status-reports-the-commits-no-bookmark-reaches). Whether they move
  up ahead of it, or delete's cycle builds the verdict as its first rung, is open.
- One experiment wants wink starting a fresh Claude Code session, the symlink's below.

#### symlink names a path over 200 characters as Claude Code does

(2026-10-09) Claude Code cuts a project name longer than 200 characters to 200 and appends `-` and
a base-36 hash of the path, and `encode_path` returns the uncut name, so `vc-x1 symlink` makes a
link Claude Code never reads for such a path. Found in the installed Claude Code (2.1.295) during
the cycle "fix: symlink names a project as Claude Code does", which left it out: the hash function
has to be copied exactly, and no path met so far is near 200.

Whether the hash has to match bit for bit is not known, and the opening tests it before any code is
written. On a scratch project whose full path is over 200 characters, wink starting a fresh Claude
Code session there for each pass:

- No link: the name Claude Code creates under `~/.claude/projects` is the ground truth, and a test
  vector for the hash if one is needed.
- The link as `vc-x1 symlink` makes it today, the uncut name: expected to be ignored, Claude Code
  creating its own directory beside it as it did for the `io_uring` project, whose link was wrong
  within the first 200 characters.

content.content:
#### delete removes a workspace from this machine

- It removes the directories and the symlink, and leaves the remote alone. A repo on the remote
  is deleted by hand.
- Its prompt lists what goes and the commits that are nowhere else.
- What stops it is below.

#### rename renames a workspace, its remote included

- It renames the repos on the remote too. The remote cannot be lost by it: the remote's rename
  happens or is refused, so the repo is under the old name or the new one.
- The remote goes first, so a refusal (the name taken, no permission) leaves the local side as it
  was. The order after it: both `origin` URLs, the configs, a commit and push in both repos, the
  directory, the symlink.
- The new name is checked as [init refuses a name GitHub would
  change](#init-refuses-a-name-github-would-change) checks one, so the URL written is the name
  the remote took.
- A run that stopped between the two repos is run again: it finds which repo has the new name
  and goes on from there.
- A workspace with no remote skips the remote steps. A remote that is not GitHub's is refused.
- Left out, and listed by the command: the name as the family's other repos hold it, the
  template, the messages, and the other members' configs.
- Open: whether it takes the workspace whole or one side at a time. One side alone overlaps
  [repos.agent becomes repos.agent-dir, and a command brings a config up to
  date](#reposagent-becomes-reposagent-dir-and-a-command-brings-a-config-up-to-date).
- Open: whether `.vc-config.toml` is still a form the commands handle.

#### What stops delete and rename

- An agent running in the workspace is not looked for. No lock is asked for, the session's being
  off and the one `vc-x1` was to take for a run not added ([vc-x1 takes a lock of its own for a
  run that writes](notes/todo-backlog.md#vc-x1-takes-a-lock-of-its-own-for-a-run-that-writes)).
- Uncommitted work, or unpushed work on a bookmark, refuses. This is the status verdict, called
  and not written again. The agent-repo's `@` is clean only after the session exits and a
  `squash-push`.
- Two findings warn and need a yes, `--yes` on the command line or `Y` at the prompt, an agent
  with no terminal using the flag as it does for push:
  - Commits no bookmark reaches.
  - A half-made workspace, a repo with no remote at all, as an `init` that failed before
    publishing leaves. Everything in it is unpushed, and it is the cleanup delete is wanted for.
- We think the two warnings are delete's alone: such commits move with the directory in a rename.

content.text:
I committed rung 4 (work `tpzuvumr`, agent `nvutuqyy`), locally. Rung 5, **feat: rung commit without a cycle** (0.85.26-5), is done and ready for review. Full validation passes, the rehearsal passes 80/80, and the dev build is reinstalled from the working copy.

**What rung 5 does:**
- **The three cases:**
  - With a cycle in progress, `rung commit` works as before, and `--title` is refused.
  - With no cycle, `--title` commits `@` as a cycle of its own.
  - A bare `rung commit` with no cycle is refused, and the message names both `cycle plan` and `--title`.
- **The verbatim form:** `rung commit -s b --title ... --body ...` makes the bookmark on `@` (the title's slug, or `--bookmark`) and commits the pair exactly as given. `TODO.md` and `zTOC.md` are left alone and don't need to exist. `main` is untouched until the Land.
- **`--record`:**
  - It runs the same planning code as `cycle plan`, without its "now plan the cycle" hint.
  - It makes the record the one heading, fills Problem and Solution from the body, and sets the Acceptance check to `_None._`.
  - It then commits through the single-step code, so the record is closed in the same commit.
- **`--land <TARGET>`** lands the commit in the same invocation, and `--push` then publishes the target. It also works on a single-step's one rung, and is refused on a ladder's rung, which `cycle close --land` covers.
- **Every check runs before the bookmark is made:** body present, `@` not empty, the version check, and the Land's checks. A refusal leaves nothing behind.
- **Tests:** two new tests: the verbatim form landed with `cycle land`, and `--record --land main`. The rehearsal gains cycle 5 (verbatim with `--land main --push`) and cycle 6 (`--record`).
- **Docs:** README gains **A commit without a cycle** under `### rung`; the help and the record are updated.

**On deleting local workspaces:** a design already existed inside **Improve init and add rename and delete subcommands**: remove the directories and symlink, leave remotes alone, prompt with what goes, refuse on unpushed work. Its order put the `init` fixes first, though, so I filed a new entry **feat: vc-x1 delete removes a workspace from this machine** second in `## Todo`, right after file-set.
- It adds your rule: local bare test repos are deleted only when asked, with a flag like `--test-repos` (name open). A remote reached by a URL, GitHub or any other host, is never touched.
- It points to the existing design for the prompt and the stop conditions, and that design's delete bullet now mentions the test-repo exception.

Please review.

It worked as designed. Here's what the `ochid` points at:

- **With `-s w` only the work half is committed.** Its `ochid:` names the agent repo's current `@`, `nopttlrpxvmp`, which is the session's journal and not yet committed. When `vc-x1 push -s b` (or `commit -s a --covers`) runs later, it commits that `@` as the partner, so the trailer ends up naming a real agent commit. That's the "work half now, agent half at push" pairing (N:1) the rules allow.
- **In this workspace that `@` is empty.** No Claude Code session has run there, so there's no transcript, and the partner would be an empty journal commit.
- **`lookup` is right.** It followed `abc.txt:1` to `zvmvtpokosov`, then the `ochid:` to the partner, and searched the partner's session data for the Write, Edit or Bash call that produced the line. There isn't one, because you ran `echo` yourself. "write none found" is the true answer for a hand-made edit.

Two things this raises:
1. **`lookup` could say why.** "no Write, Edit, or Bash call carries the line" reads the same whether the partner has no session at all or has one that didn't write the line. It could say "the partner holds no session data, so the line was not written by an agent" in the first case. That's a small Todo if you want it.
2. **A human-only commit still gets an agent partner.** I'd keep that: every work commit stays linked, push stays uniform, and the empty partner is cheap. The alternative is no `ochid:` when the agent `@` is empty, but then a later session's journal would have nothing to attach to. I'd leave it as is.

**Your body text lost its backticks again.** Inside double quotes the shell ran `` `echo abc > abc.txt` `` as a command substitution, so the body reads "Created abc.txt with " and `abc.txt` was rewritten. Single quotes keep it literal.

You're right, and I'll withdraw that wording. `lookup` can never conclude "not written by an agent", even when the agent repo is completely empty. The line could have come from an agent in another workspace, a script an agent ran, or a tool outside Claude Code. An empty partner only means the partner records no write. It should report what it searched and what it found, and never guess who wrote the line.

Your two cases:
- **With `-s b`:** the empty agent `@` would have been committed then, as an empty partner commit. `lookup` follows the `ochid:` to it, finds no session data, so there's no window, and you get the same "write none found". Nothing more to go on.
- **With `-s a` later** (`commit -s a --covers`, or the push): the same change, `nopttlrpxvmp`, is committed then, holding whatever the journal has gathered by that point, possibly sessions that ran after the work commit.
  - If a later session wrote the same text to `abc.txt`, `lookup` would find that write and mark it "(after the window, a later amend)". It's flagged as later, but it isn't where the line came from.
  - If no later session touched it, it's "none found" again.

So the message is already factual. It just doesn't say what was searched, which is what would let you weigh it. What it could say instead:
- `partner nopttlrpxvmp (the agent @, not committed yet)` when the partner is still the working copy.
- `write none found: the partner holds no session data` when there's nothing to search.
- `write none found: N entries searched, no Write, Edit, or Bash call on abc.txt carries the line` when there is.

All three are facts about the search, with no claim about who wrote the line. Should I file that as a Todo? Rung 5 is still waiting for your review.

163:- **`cycle squash` makes a ladder one commit** (wink, 2026-11-20): the work rungs squashed into the
164-  opening, whose change id jj keeps, under the bare title, the record moved to `## Closed` as a
165-  single-step's.
166-  - The agent side is re-pointed, not squashed: each agent commit's `ochid:` rewritten to the one
167-    work commit, and that commit's naming every agent commit, the 1:M shape the agent-files already
168-    allow. Only descriptions change, so the change ids the work commit names stay, and the
169-    agent-repo keeps its per-rung history. Squashing the agent side too was simpler and lost that.
170-  - The agent side is rewritten first, then the work side.
171-  - Refused, with no override, over a work rung a target reaches, its history permanent. A work
172-    rung that is only draft-pushed is rewritten, and the next push of the bookmark is a forced push,
173-    asked about as today.
174-  - Refused without `--yes` over an agent commit `main@origin` reaches: the agent-repo has no draft
175-    bookmark, a draft push moving the agent `main` (`src/push.rs`), so the rewrite is a forced push
176-    of `main`, which another machine's clone would diverge from.
177-  - The rule **A ladder lands as a trapezoid, never squashed** gives way, its reason, the lost
178-    change ids, answered by the re-point.
179-  - It takes the long single-step too, a branch of the opening alone or none, so `cycle close`'s
180-    `--single-step` and `--multi-step` and the commit-count check go with it, `close` always a
181-    ladder's closing and the shape said by the headings or by the verb.
182-- **The stages are subcommands** (wink, 2026-11-19): `cycle
183-  plan|close|squash|land|push|status|ladder` and `rung next|stop|commit`, a cycle's acts and a
184-  rung's each a command of their own.
185-  - The flags were for chaining, `cycle --close --land main`, which a subcommand keeps with its
186-    later stages as flags, `cycle close --land main --push`.
187-  - `plan` over `open` (wink): the stage is the plan's, deliberated before its commit.
188-  - No compatibility (wink): the old flags go without a warning, since no other cycle is in flight
189-    and none starts before the proposal is done.
190-  - This record names the stages as they were when each line was written.

194-The rung subsections, in the ladder's order. The ladder itself is in `zTOC.md > ## Ladder`.

as on every command that writes, and the other stages take none.

a ladder through these subcommands, plan to Land, checks what each command left, and tries each way
back from a fault found after a closing, naming the ones the tool refuses. `VC` names the binary,
`vc-x1-dev` by default.

p='README.md'
lines=open(p).read().split('\n')
def reflow_at(idx):
    # find the bullet/paragraph containing line idx (0-based)
    start=idx
    while start>0 and lines[start-1].strip()!='' and not lines[start].startswith('- ') and not lines[start].startswith('|') :
        start-=1
    end=idx
    while end+1<len(lines) and lines[end+1].strip()!='' and not lines[end+1].startswith('- '):
        end+=1
    first=lines[start]
    bullet=first.startswith('- ')
    prefix='- ' if bullet else ''
    cont='  ' if bullet else ''
    text=' '.join(l.strip() for l in lines[start:end+1])
    if bullet: text=text[2:]
    words=text.split(' ')
    out=[];cur=prefix
    for w in words:
        base = prefix if not out else cont
        if cur.strip() and len(cur)+1+len(w)>100:
            out.append(cur); cur=cont+w
        else:
            cur = cur+w if cur in (prefix,cont) else cur+' '+w
    out.append(cur)
    lines[start:end+1]=out
for n in sorted([1817,1853,1997],reverse=True):
    reflow_at(n-1)
open(p,'w').write('\n'.join(lines))
EOF

**`cycle squash`** is a new stage that makes the cycle one commit under the bare title:
- **What it does, by what the branch holds:**
  - No commit: the work `@` is committed as the one commit.
  - The opening alone: `@` is folded into the opening.
  - The opening plus work rungs:
    - The agent side goes first. Each agent commit that names a rung gets only its description rewritten, so it names the opening. The agent repo keeps its per-rung history.
    - The opening then gets an `ochid:` for every agent commit, and each rung is squashed into it oldest first, which keeps the opening's change id.
    - Finally the same single-step fold writes the record into `## Closed` without `#### Rungs`, the ladder as `0 (done) <title>`, and the bare title.
- **Checked before anything is rewritten:**
  - The first commit is the opening, and the bookmark is on `@` or `@-`.
  - No rung is started except the closing.
  - No conflicts, the version check, and the Land's checks.
  - No branch commit is reached by a remote bookmark other than the cycle's own; its draft push is fine.
  - No agent commit on the agent `main@origin` is rewritten without `--yes`.
- **Failure:** if anything fails, both repos are restored.
- **Options:** `--body` is required, or `--default-body` for the pointer at the record. `-s` is `b` or `p`. `--land` and `--push` chain as on `close`.

**`cycle close`** loses `--single-step`, `--multi-step`, `--default-body` and the commit-count check. It is now always a ladder's closing, and it's refused with no opening committed, naming `squash`. The single-step code stays inside `close` for `squash`, a single-step's one rung and `rung commit --record`. `cycle status` now suggests `squash` where it used to suggest `--single-step`.

- **Rehearsal:** cycles 1 and 2 use `squash`, cycle 3 drops `--multi-step`, and a new cycle 7 squashes a ladder and checks the trailers in both repos.

**README:** the `close` section loses its shape table, and `squash` gets its own section with the three cases.

content.text:
Assuming the heading is `##### feat: create abc.txt` under `#### Rungs`, between the opening and the closing:

```bash
vc-x1-dev cycle ladder                 # rewrite zTOC.md from the headings
vc-x1-dev rung next                    # start the opening, the plan
vc-x1-dev rung commit -s b             # commit the plan; the opening's title and body are filled in for you
vc-x1-dev rung next                    # start 'feat: create abc.txt'
echo abc > abc.txt
vc-x1-dev rung commit -s b --body 'Why.

Solution: how.'                        # commit the rung
```

Then finish the cycle one of two ways:
- **Keep the ladder:** `vc-x1-dev cycle close -s b`, then `vc-x1-dev cycle land main -s b --push`.
- **Make it one commit:** `vc-x1-dev cycle squash -s b --body '...' --land main --push`.

Notes:
- **`--ver`:** your test workspace has no `[version]` in its config, so leave it off. With a bump configured, you'd give `--ver X.Y.Z-0` on the first `rung next` and `--ver X.Y.Z-1` on the second.
- **Where you are:** `vc-x1-dev cycle status` shows it at any point. It names the started rung and the command that commits it.
- **Quoting:** use single quotes around a `--body` with backticks in it.

I like it. It makes the plan a phase of its own, which it really is: the opening isn't work, it's the plan, and starting and committing it with `rung next` / `rung commit` hides that. Your flow, with what each step would do:

```
cycle plan start --title "..."   # bookmark + record scaffold (today's `cycle plan`)
  ... deliberate, write rung headings ...
cycle plan commit -s b           # ladder from the headings, then the opening committed
rung next / work / rung commit   # each work rung
cycle close | cycle squash       # a ladder's closing, or one commit
```
or, for a one-off: `cycle plan start`, do the work, `cycle squash`.

Points in its favour:
- **`plan commit` absorbs `cycle ladder`.** The ladder is always rewritten from the headings before the opening is committed, so the usual flow needs no separate ladder step. `cycle ladder` stays for inserting a rung mid-cycle.
- **The opening is never `(current)`.** `rung next` only ever starts work rungs, and refuses before the plan is committed, naming `cycle plan commit`.
- **`start`/`commit` mirrors `rung next`/`rung commit`.** Each phase has a beginning and a commit.
- **The squash-only path already works.** `squash` with no commit on the branch commits `@` as the one commit, so `plan start` then `squash` needs nothing new.

Things to decide:
- **The version:** I'd put `--ver X.Y.Z-0` on `plan start`. That keeps the rule that the bump comes at a step's start, so the reviewed tree carries it. The record's line "`cycle plan` changes no version" would change.
- **Rung 4's one-heading single-step:** with `plan start` then `squash` giving the same one commit, the simple style (bare `--ver` rewriting the bookends into one heading) may be redundant. Only the record's look during the cycle differs. It could be dropped, or kept for `rung commit --record`, which uses it internally.
- **The name for "start":** `plan start` reads well beside `plan commit`, though `plan` alone could also mean start. Two explicit verbs are clearer.

The plain version: making the plan its own two steps, start then commit, removes the odd part of treating the opening as a rung. The rest of the flow already fits, including the squash-only shortcut. It would be a new rung before the docs rung, after rung 6 is committed. Rung 6 is still waiting for your review.

content.content:
### cycle

Run a cycle by its stages, each a subcommand, beside [`rung`](#rung)'s acts, which run each rung
from the opening on: `plan`, then `rung next` and `rung commit` for each rung, then `close`, or
`squash` to make the cycle one commit, `land`, and `push`, with `ladder` to rewrite the ladder and
`status` to say where the cycle stands. A later stage chains as a flag, so `cycle close -s b
--land main --push` closes, lands, and publishes in one invocation. `-s` is required with `close`,
`squash`, `land`, and `push`, as on every command that writes, and the other stages take none.

```bash
vc-x1 cycle plan --title "feat: a cycle"                # the bookmark, and the record
vc-x1 cycle plan --title "feat: a cycle" --no-record    # the bookmark alone
vc-x1 cycle plan --title "feat: a cycle" --dry-run      # say each edit, make none
vc-x1 cycle ladder                                      # the ladder, from the rung headings
vc-x1 rung next --ver 0.86.0-0                          # start the opening, its version set
vc-x1 rung commit -s b                                  # the opening, a cycle's first commit
vc-x1 rung next --ver 0.86.0-1                          # start the next rung
vc-x1 rung commit -s b --body @body.txt                 # a work rung
vc-x1 cycle close -s b                                  # a ladder's closing, linear
vc-x1 cycle close -s b --trapezoid main                 # a merge, main its first parent
vc-x1 cycle squash -s b --body @body.txt                # the cycle made one commit
vc-x1 cycle land main -s b                              # land the closed cycle, locally
vc-x1 cycle land main -s b --push                       # and publish it
vc-x1 cycle push -s b                                   # publish what the cycle's state calls for
vc-x1 cycle close -s b --trapezoid main --land main --push  # close, land, publish
vc-x1 cycle land main -s b --merge                      # join a main that moved, then land
vc-x1 cycle status                                      # where the cycle stands, and what is next
```

`plan` opens a cycle. It makes the bookmark on the work `@` first, so every edit of the cycle
is on its branch, and then writes the cycle's record into the working copy. The bookmark is the
slug of `--title`, the anchor a heading of the title gets: lowercase, `-` and `_` kept, each space
a `-`, everything else dropped, so `feat: no trunk, every target is named` names
`feat-no-trunk-every-target-is-named`. `--bookmark` names it instead. A name in use, locally or on
`origin`, is refused, since a new one would move or shadow it. `@` may hold edits, which become
the opening's, a `main` not where its `origin` was last fetched is a warning, the agent repo gets
no bookmark, being on `main` alone, and nothing is pushed. The record:

- In `TODO.md`, what `## Closed` holds is deleted, its intro kept, and the `## Todo` entry titled
  as `--title` is moved into an `## In Progress` scaffold: the title, the item headings, the
  entry's text under Problem, and the opening and closing rung subsections. No entry of that title
  is an empty scaffold, and says so.
- In `zTOC.md`, the ladder is replaced with the opening and the closing, neither marked, the
  opening started by [`rung next`](#rung).
- A workspace with no `TODO.md` or no `zTOC.md`, one made before `vc-x1 init` wrote them, gets the
  skeleton `init` writes first: `TODO.md` with `## Continuation notes`, `## In Progress`, `## Todo`,
  and `## Closed`, and `zTOC.md` with `## Ladder`. A file there is kept as it is.

Everything is planned before anything is made, so a cycle in progress, a `TODO.md` with no `## In
Progress`, and a name in use are each refused with the workspace as it was. `--no-record` and
`--bookmark` without `--title` get the bookmark alone, a branch that `rung commit` and `close`
will not take, since they read the cycle from its record. Nothing
is committed or pushed, and the version is the project's to bump, by hand or by `rung next --ver`.
A
reference definition only `## Closed` cited is left, for `check anchors` to name. `-R` is
optional and says where, a workspace or a plain repo.

`ladder` makes the ladder in `zTOC.md` from the rung headings of the cycle in progress, the
`##### ` headings under `#### Rungs` in `TODO.md`, in their order. A rung is written once, as its

I added **feat: cycle plan start and commit** as rung 7, after `cycle squash`. When I first inserted it I accidentally dropped the docs rung's heading; I put it back, and the ladder now lists every rung in order. I then committed rung 6 (work `ovooponm`, agent `znoptqxq`), locally.

Rung 7 (0.85.26-7) is done and ready for review. Full validation passes, the rehearsal passes 91/91, and the dev build is reinstalled from the working copy.

**What changed:**
- **`cycle plan start`** is the old `cycle plan`: bookmark plus record. It gains `--ver X.Y.Z-0`, which runs the config's bump last, so a refusal bumps nothing and the plan under review carries the version. Its closing hint now says `cycle plan commit -s <SCOPE>` commits the plan.
- **`cycle plan commit -s b`** commits the plan as the opening, with the title and body filled in for you. It rewrites the ladder from the headings into the commit, so there's no need to run `cycle ladder` first. It's refused when the plan is already committed, and on a one-heading plan, which has no opening.
- **`rung next`** never starts the opening now. Before the plan is committed it refuses and names `cycle plan commit`. The one exception is the bare-`--ver` shortcut, which still turns the plan into the one heading and starts it.
- **`cycle status`** suggests `cycle plan commit` before the opening, and `cycle plan start` when there's no cycle.

**Your flow now works as written:**
```
cycle plan start --title "..."   (deliberate, add rung headings)
cycle plan commit -s b
rung next / work / rung commit -s b --body ...
cycle close -s b  |  cycle squash -s b --body ...
```
or the one-off: `cycle plan start`, the work, then `cycle squash`.

**Tests:**
- The rung-flow test now commits the plan with `plan commit` and checks that `rung next` refuses before it.
- The old opening-started single-step test is now `a_one_off_squashes_after_plan_start`.
- There's a new test for `plan start --ver` and for `plan commit` refusing a one-heading plan.
- The rehearsal commits every plan with `plan commit`.

**Docs:** README's `### cycle` shows the two plan steps, with a `plan commit` paragraph, and the help texts are updated.

Still open, noted in the rung: whether to drop rung 4's one-heading single-step, since `plan start` then `squash` now covers the one-off.

Please review.
